News.title: Ukraine blitzes MORE ‘Russian Amazon’ logistics hubs as vids show two vast warehouses ablaze in blow to Putin’s economy
News.content:
UKRAINE has launched a fresh barrage of strikes on “Russia’s Amazon” – sparking massive infernos ripping through the retail giant’s warehouses.

Key logistics hubs run by e-commerce firm Wildberries were set ablaze leaving over £1billion in damages – and another setback for Vladimir Putin.



The attacks on Wildberries – a platform accused of propping up Putin’s war machine – mark another huge blow to Russia’s flailing economy.

Jaw-dropping images showed towering columns of black smoke rising into the skies while vicious fires tore through the retailer’s complexes.



The assault is part of Ukraine’s endgame blitz – a series of deep strikes targeting energy and logistics hubs in Russia.

Kyiv hopes severe disruption to daily life will turn the Russian people against Putin and pressure the tyrant towards peace.

Last night’s strikes hit critical hubs in Krasnodar and Nevinnomyssk, both in Western Russia.

They came just days after two separate Wildberries hubs were struck, in Elektrostal near Moscow, and Tambov, causing £1.5billion in damages.



At least 10 people were wounded in the Krasnodar attack.

A firefighting helicopter was deployed to tackle the massive blaze in Krasnodar, capital of a region where three other Putin palaces are located.

After the blitz on Nevinnomyssk, a state of emergency was declared in Stavropol region.



Thick black plumes of smoke could be seen rising from both warehouse complexes which are 148 miles apart.

Huge infernos could be seen tearing through the buildings – key cogs in Putin’s bloody invasion.

Wildberries is owned by Putin-backing Tatyana Kim, 50, Russia’s richest woman with a £6.1billion fortune.



The crippling fires, which were sparked at the fourth and sixth largest Wildberries bases in Russia, highlight Putin’s struggling air defences.

One desperate supplier to the retail giant said: “Many will wake up bankrupt today.”

A resident of Nevinnomyssk in Stavropol region pleaded: “Putin – end this war now.”

Additionally, a major oil depot was set ablaze at Armavir in Krasnodar after being attacked by a swarm of at least 16 Ukrainian drones.

At least one person died in the assault which was aimed at exacerbating Russia’s chronic oil shortages.



Meanwhile, Russian-occupied Crimea was hit by fresh blackouts after the another round of Ukrainian strikes on power plants.

The Black Sea peninsula that Putin annexed in 2014 has been subject to a drone and missile campaign aimed at isolating the territory from Russia’s mainland.

The attacks come as Ukraine continues to shift the momentum of the war in its favour.

And they also came hours after Volodymyr Zelensky fired his Commander-in-Chief Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi, 60.

He has been replaced by Maj-Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi, 43 – a younger figure seen as more willing to embrace modernisation of the army, including drones and AI.



Syrskyi was nicknamed “The Butcher” for his readiness to defend the frontlines leading to human losses.

He said on Wednesday he had reclaimed 270 square miles of Ukrainian territory this year from the Russian invaders.

Drapatyi has argued that Ukraine can better defend itself with a more concentrated use of the country’s new high-powered drones and missiles.

It comes as Putin continues to launch strikes on Ukrainian civilians.

Russia struck a Nova Poshta – a major delivery service – logistics centre in Odesa, and the city’s port overnight.

Five people including three children were also injured in a Russian strike on the Kyiv region.

News.title: Brit from Isle of Wight becomes world’s most senior foreign-born Buddhist monk after 50-year search for enlightenment
News.content:
FEELING ZEN Brit from Isle of Wight becomes world’s most senior foreign-born Buddhist monk after 50-year search for enlightenment

A BRITISH man born on the Isle of Wight has made history as the world’s most senior foreign-born Buddhist monk.

Shaun Michael Chiverton, 68, now sits just one tier below the Supreme Patriarch in Thailand’s Buddhist monastery after a 50-year search for enlightenment.



Now known as monk Ajahn Jayasaro, Shaun was appointed to Somdet Phra Rachakhana under a momentous royal decree.

The esteemed move marks the first foreign-born monk in Thailand’s history to be elevated to the senior monastic rank.



Shaun was gifted the religious promotion by King Vajiralongkorn alongside seven other senior monks, according to a decree published in Thailand’s Royal Gazette on July 14.

There are nine tiers in the Theravada monastic hierarchy with Shaun now in the second highest.



He has been described as “one of Thailand’s most respected contemporary Buddhist teachers,” by the Bangkok Post.

The Brit’s unique journey to find enlightenment through Buddhism started in the 1970s as he started to research Buddhist philosophy as a teen.

He spent years studying in England under British-born monk Ajahn Sumedho all while he saved up cash so he could jet out to Thailand.

In 1979, Shaun made the jump as he became fully immersed in the world of Theravada Buddhism.



Theravada is the second largest branch of Buddhism in the world with up 36 per cent of global Buddhist followers following the practices.

Shaun entered as a disciple of Luang Por Chah Subhaddo – one of Thailand’s most revered meditation masters.

Within 18 months, he managed to take on full monkhood.



He was given the name Jayasaro which translates in English to “one who is victorious through the dhamma”.

The Brit spent the next five years practicing Buddhism before taking part in the traditional dhutanga ascetic practices in a forest retreat.

A 16-year stint saw him rise through the ranks at Wat Pah Nanachat, the International Forest Monastery.

Here he served as deputy abbot and later as abbot – a monk who has been elected to serve as the spiritual and administrative leader of a monastery.

He would leave his role as head of the monastery in 2003 to live a solitary life at a forest hermitage in Nakhon Ratchasima.



This led him to focus on becoming a teacher of meditation as well as writing several books in English and Thai to help new worshippers.

In 2011, he received an honorary doctorate in Buddhist Communications from Thailand’s Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

He was also granted Thai citizenship in 2020 by King Vajiralongkorn in recognition of his contributions to Buddhism.



Shaun’s decades of hard work and teachings were rewarded as he quickly rose through Thailand’s religious ranks with three promotions in the past seven years.

One of these came in 2024, as he was awarded the rank of deputy Somdet Phra Ratchakhana under the title Phra Phrom Phatcharayanamuni.

Within two years, he became Somdet Phra Ratchakhana – dropping the deputy – in the historic announcement earlier this month.

Thailand is a predominantly Theravada Buddhist country, with 92.5 per cent the population identifying as Buddhists.

The country, often cited as a tourist hotspot, has 44,195 officially registered temples, including 311 royal temples.



There are an estimated 300,000 Buddhist monks across the nation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The largest branch of Buddhists remains Mahayana Buddhism which accounts for over 50 per cent of Buddhists worldwide.

They are often seen in China, Japan, South Korea and Vietnam.

News.title: Wreckage of Pan Am plane crash that killed 52 finally found 2,000ft underwater more than seven decades after disaster
News.content:
WATERY GRAVE Wreckage of Pan Am plane crash that killed 52 finally found 2,000ft underwater more than seven decades after disaster

THE wreckage of a Pan Am plane crash that killed 52 people has finally been found 2,000ft underwater after nearly a quarter of a century.

The Clipper Endeavour lost both its right-side engines and plunged into the Atlantic Ocean off the northern coast of Puerto Rico on April 11, 1952.



It crashed only ten minutes after taking off, bound for what is now JFK International Airport in New York.

The Douglas DC-4 aircraft, which is roughly the same size as a modern Boeing 737, was carrying 64 passengers and five crew members.



While everyone survived the violent impact, only 12 passengers and the five crew survived.

Pre-flight safety briefings were not standard at the time, leading to mass panic and confusion in the cabin.

As such, many passengers struggled to find their life vests and the crew struggled to pull rafts out.

The fuselage was pulled under the surface within just three minutes and 52 people drowned.

Its wreckage has been unreachable for 74 years due to its depth, but after years of trying, explorers finally made a breakthrough.

The Air/Sea Heritage Foundation, as well as Discovery Channel’s Expedition Unknown series, found the wreckage off the coast of Puerto Rican capital San Juan on June 2, Discovery said on Tuesday.



The Foundation partnered with an Eco Minerals Company called Deep Sea Vision who provided the high-resolution sonar capable of scanning to incredible depths.

They used autonomous underwater vehicles that were able to search at depths of up to 20,000ft while staying submerged for up to four days at a time.

Russ Matthews, president of the Air/Sea Heritage Foundation, said: “We are all stunned and elated by this discovery yet also humbled to remember what happened in that place so long ago.”

In 2019, Russ launched his search for the Clipper Endeavour after stumbling on a blurb about a luggage tag from the flight washing up on Florida’s shores.



He teamed up with Expedition Unknown host Josh Gates in 2024 for an episode, uncovering crucial hidden evidence that included a chart map created by US Air Force pilots who saw the crash.

Josh said in a statement: “Seeing the bright aluminium fuselage shining back at us from the ocean floor was a hugely emotional moment.”

It was found broken in two sections, with the Pan Am logo still clearly visible.

While the plane disappeared for decades, the disaster led to major aviation reforms, making pre-flight safety briefings standard and emergency procedure demonstrations.

Thousands of lives are believed to have been saved by the reforms in the ensuing 74 years.



Josh said: “Every time you step on board an aeroplane today, you are safer because of what happened to Clipper Endeavour and her passengers three quarters of a century ago.

“This aircraft vanished beneath the waves, and the legacy of those aboard was at risk of being lost with it.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I hope this historic discovery brings some peace to the families of those aboard and serves to remind the flying public today of the debt of remembrance we owe to this fateful flight.”

An episode of its “Expedition Unknown” series is expected to cover the discovery later this year.

News.title: Mass 10-person brawl on easyJet flight to UK forces plane to turn back to Tenerife for emergency landing
News.content:
MID-AIR CHAOS Mass 10-person brawl on easyJet flight to UK forces plane to turn back to Tenerife for emergency landing

A MASSIVE 10-person brawl has erupted on an easyJet flight to the UK – forcing the plane to turn back and emergency land in Tenerife.

The scuffle broke out in front of terrified passengers on a Liverpool-bound aircraft last night before it returned to the holiday hotspot.



The sprawling bust-up unfolded on flight EZY3352 which departed from Tenerife South Airport just before 8pm local time on Tuesday.

The fight was so intense that the pilot had to turn back due to the “danger this posed to the safety of the flight”, authorities said.



Flight tracking data shows the jet returned to the same airport at 9:05pm.

It is not clear whether the passengers accused of being in the fight were British, or if any were arrested.



Spanish air traffic authorities said: “The crew of the flight from Tenerife South to Liverpool informed us, after about 30 minutes in the air, that they needed to return to the airport and requested a police presence upon arrival.

“A group of around 10 passengers had started a fight on board, and the captain decided to turn back because of the danger this posed to the safety of the flight.”

They added: “We expedited their return as much as possible while coordinating with the airport to ensure a police presence.

“They landed and vacated runway 07 without incident.



“Our full support goes to the crews and passengers who are having to endure these situations more and more often.”

It comes after shocking footage showed the extraordinary moment an easyJet captain wrestled a boozed-up passenger to the floor on a holiday jet.

The white-shirted hero pilot and a brave crew member tussled with the allegedly drunken yob in the rear galley of a packed plane.

And in May, a drunk man and woman were arrested on an easyJet plane from Gatwick to Antalya in Turkey.

Passengers said the woman was swigging from a bottle of vodka, spat at someone and that there was a fight.



The man allegedly bragged he had been in jail and said anyone moaning about them would be killed.

PARK HORROR Teenage girl ‘sexually assaulted’ in park near Premier League stadium in broad daylight attack – as cops launch probe

COPS are investigating reports that a teenage girl was sexually assaulted in a park near Old Trafford yesterday afternoon.

Officers rushed to the scene shortly before 6pm after the alleged attack in Victoria Park in Stretford, Manchester.



They cordoned off parts of the park, including a footpath and an area of woodland, while detectives began their enquiries.

Greater Manchester Police said no arrests have been made and confirmed the alleged victim is being supported by officers.



A force spokesperson said: “Greater Manchester Police is investigating a report of sexual assault that occurred shortly before 6pm (21/07/2026) in Victoria Park, Stretford.

“No arrests have been made at this time.



“However, the victim is being supported and detectives are following up multiple lines of enquiry to piece together the full circumstances.”

News.title: Fury as Wes Streeting & Shabana Mahmood caught on hot mic joking about Labour’s early prison release scheme
News.content:
WES Streeting and Shabana Mahmood have landed in hot water after they were caught on a hot mic joking about Labour’s early prison release scheme.

Embarassing footage shows the two Cabinet ministers joking with new Justice minister Alex Norris, with Streeting saying: “He wants to let them all out”.



The duo were caught on a hot mic after new PM Andy Burnham‘s first Cabinet meeting – with the poor taste gaffe coming just one day into the new look Government.

And their comments have sparked fury, with Reform MP Robert Jenrick saying: “The real pain and suffering early prison release has caused so many people is clearly funny to the Labour Party.”



Mr Streeting has since apologised in a post online, saying “it was a reference to an old May/Clarke joke”, while Mahmood said there was “no ill intent.”

It also came just hours before it emerged PC Andrew Harper’s killers are set for early release.



Labour have released almost 40,000 criminals from prison early since September 2024 – saying they need to ease overcrowding.

In footage of the gaffe, Mr Streeting can be heard saying: “You know he’s [Alex Norris] the enemy now, Justice Shabana?”



Ms Mahmood replied: “No he’s not!”

The new Defence Secretary said: “He wants to let them all out.”

Ms Mahmood then responded: “You know who’s boss!”

The Ministry of Justice figures show 38,042 were freed under the scheme between September 2024 and June 2025.

Labour introduced the scheme after prisons almost reached full capacity – with the government saying the inherited a crisis of overcrowding.



Under the emergency measures some inmates are released after serving 40 per cent of their fixed term sentence.

Reform Shadow Chancellor Robert Jenrick was not impressed with the Cabinet ministers’ joke and took to social media to slam the duo – brandingthemn “out of touch.”

He said: “Wes Streeting and Shabana Mahmood have been caught laughing about letting prisoners out early.



“Last year someone died after a prisoner released early killed them the same day. But the real pain and suffering early prison release has caused so many people is clearly funny to the Labour Party.

“They were caught out joking in the Number 10 garden as they congratulated themselves on their new jobs. They could not be more out of touch from the real world.

“Truly rotten behaviour.

“Only Reform UK can shake up the rotten establishment.”

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch also wrote in a statement: “While Andy Burnham’s cabinet are joking about letting criminals out of prison early, Conservatives are listening to victims and will continue to fight this disgusting policy.”



Susan Hall, the leader of the Tories on the London Assembly, said: “The early release from Prison of murderers, rapists , grooming gang members is a disgrace in itself.

“Anyone laughing about should not be in Labours Government.”

After the opposition’s dressing down, Streeting and Mahmood both apologised for “ribbing” Norris about the early release scheme.

Mr Streeting said in a post online: “I hope everyone can see there was no ill intent behind this ribbing of the new justice secretary – it was a reference to an old May/Clarke joke.

“But I appreciate these are very serious issues and am sorry for any offence inadvertently caused by this moment of levity.”



Streeting was referencing comments between former Tory home secretary Theresa May and justice secretary Kenneth Clarke.

May joked she “locked ‘em up and he let ‘em out” when explaining the roles.

The Home Secretary also posted online: “I think everyone can see there was no ill intent behind this ribbing of the new lord chancellor – a role I once filled and which comes with immense challenges thanks to the vandalism inflicted on our justice system by the last Conservative government.

“But I appreciate this is an extremely serious issue and do not want anyone to mistake this moment of levity for a lack of serious intent.”

Hours before the footage emerged it was revealed that two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers could be set for an early release from jail under Labour’s plans.



Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were jailed for 13 years in 2020 for the manslaughter of the 28-year-old officer.

The pair, who were 17 at the time of the offence in August 2019, were passengers in the car that dragged PC Harper for more than a mile along country roads when his ankles got caught in a towrope loop.

He had gone to investigate the theft of a quad bike when Bowers and Cole tried to escape in a vehicle driven by a third killer, Henry Long.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

PC Harper sustained serious injuries and died in the road.

But the pair are now eligible to be freed just halfway through their sentences under the Ministry of Justice early release scheme.

News.title: Waitrose urgently recalls £1.50 bakery staple that ‘could contain hard plastic and METAL’
News.content:
WAITROSE has pulled a popular bakery item from shelves over fears the pastries may contain pieces of hard plastic and metal.

If shoppers have bought the product, they have been urged not to eat them, and return the packets to their nearest store.



Waitrose has urgently recalled a batch of its 8 Chocolate Chip Brioche Rolls due to metal and hard plastic contamination.

The Food Standards Agency has alerted shoppers that the impacted batch is “unsafe to eat”.



The affected products display a best-before date of July 26, 2026, and a batch code of B26177.

Details of the batch code and best-before date can be found on the back of the packet.



Currently, no other batches of the chocolate chip brioche rolls have been recalled by the supermarket.

Waitrose has urged customers who have bought the brioche rolls to not eat any of them.

Instead, the multipack should be packaged up, then returned to a local Waitrose & Partners branch where a full refund will be issued.

Point of sale notices will also be displayed in all the Waitrose stores that have sold this product, explaining why it was recalled.



The multipack of chocolate chip brioche rolls is sold both in-stores and online for just £1.50.

Waitrose said on its recall: “We apologise that it has been necessary to recall this product and for the inconvenience caused.”

News.title: Boy, 6, died in horror crash minutes after dad suffered ‘life-changing injuries’ in separate collision – as man arrested
News.content:
'UNIMAGINABLE LOSS' Boy, 6, died in horror crash minutes after dad suffered ‘life-changing injuries’ in separate collision – as man arrested

Credit: eyJpdiI6IkNOWEJ4UkNiVklzdXZrZ2tzcjJGdkE9PSIsInZhbHVlIjoiclB3R0NLbUdRZWNnbGFieHJ2dWkrTjhBNmtQRVZuMFdzcDkweWVLUjNMM1JHcHdiWW5HSjRqb0RuR0tPd1NPa0NYbEZwa0FqOGhUb0xzMWpXQlI4d2c9PSIsIm1hYyI6IjRkMzdlMjQ5NTI1MDc5ZDVlMjdkNzg1ODI5ZmZiMmVjYmI0YTc3MjExMWQ0NjlhNjJjYTk0ZmYzMjQ4YjExNzciLCJ0YWciOiIifQ==

A BOY tragically died in a horrific crash minutes after his father suffered “life-changing” injuries.

Cohen, 6, has been pictured for the first time since he passed away six days after he was involved in a crash between a car and a van in Skellow, Doncaster.

The boy, a passenger in a white Volkswagen Golf, was left fighting for his life after it crashed into a parked white Citroen Relay van.

The terrible incident occurred on June 25, close to the junction of Poplar Road and Lodge Road.





South Yorkshire Police shared that a 52-year-old man had been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving among other motoring offences.

The man has been bailed while cops conduct further inquiries, which the van driver is assisting with.

After emergency services attended the scene, Cohen was rushed to hospital but sadly died on July 1.

Just minutes before the awful collision, Cohen’s father was knocked off his bike and suffered severe injuries.

A fundraiser has been started to support the family while they cope with the loss of their son and the father’s recovery.

So far the family has raised more than £2,000.

The fundraiser page read: “Our community is coming together to support a local family whose lives were changed forever after two devastating accidents occurred just minutes apart.

“Tragically, these heartbreaking events claimed the life of a beautiful 6-year-old boy Cohen.



“His father also suffered life-changing injuries and now faces a long and uncertain road to recovery.

“The family is left not only grieving the unimaginable loss of their little boy, but also facing the physical, emotional, and financial challenges that lie ahead.

“No family should have to endure such overwhelming heartbreak alone.

“Every donation, no matter the amount, will help ease the financial burden, allowing the family to focus on healing, recovery, and supporting one another during this incredibly difficult time.

“If you’re unable to donate, please consider sharing this post to help us reach others who may be able to help.”

News.title: EasyJet flight to UK turns back to Tenerife as mass 10-person brawl erupts in mid-air
News.content:
EasyJet flight to UK turns back to Tenerife as mass 10-person brawl erupts in mid-air

A group of passengers were involved in a mass brawl on board a flight from Tenerife to Liverpool, forcing the plane to return to the airport in Spain

View Image The fight broke out on an easyJet plane (Stock) (Image: Jam Press)

An easyJet flight bound for the UK has been forced to turn back to Tenerife after a mass fight on board.

‌



Spanish air traffic controllers said overnight 'around 10 passengers' had been involved in the fracas on board the plane heading for Liverpool.

‌



They said in a statement: “The crew of the flight from Tenerife South to Liverpool informed us, after about 30 minutes in the air, that they needed to return to the airport and requested a police presence upon arrival.

‌



“A group of around 10 passengers had started a fight on board, and the captain decided to turn back because of the danger this posed to the safety of the flight. We expedited their return as much as possible while coordinating with the airport to ensure a police presence.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

“They landed and vacated runway 07 without incident. Our full support goes to the crews and passengers who are having to endure these situations more and more often.”

‌



The incident happened on easyJet flight EZY3352, which flight trackers show left Tenerife South Airport just before 8pm local time yesterday and returned to the same airport at five minutes past nine.

It was not immediately clear this morning whether the passengers said to have been involved in the fight were all British and whether any had been arrested.

One Spaniard responding to the news said on social media: “I'm amazed by the number of flights departing from or arriving in the UK that experience security problems like this. What a disgrace.”

‌



The Mirror has contacted Spanish police for comment.

Meanwhile a flight from London Gatwick to Ibiza turned around just moments after take-off for a ‘general emergency’ this morning.

Wednesday’s 5:35am easyJet flight to the Spanish island on Wednesday morning has returned and landed safely back at London Gatwick, according to Flight Radar 24.

‌



It’s thought the plane transmitted a ‘general emergency’ code ahead of returning to its original airport. Eyewitnesses have said on social media that 'lots of fire trucks' are in attendance at the airport.

“EasyJet Flight EZY52LD turns back toward London Gatwick Airport in UK after transmitting code 7700, indicating general emergency, shortly after takeoff,” Flight Radar 24 said.

A spokesperson for easyJet said the plane, an Airbus A320-214, suffered a 'technical issue'. A statement from the company explained: “Flight EZY8099 from London Gatwick to Ibiza this morning diverted back to London Gatwick where it requested a priority landing due to a technical issue.

Article continues below

"The captain performed a routine landing in line with procedures, and the aircraft was met by emergency services at London Gatwick as a precaution only. The safety of our customers and crew is easyJet's highest priority and easyJet operates its fleet of aircraft in strict compliance with all manufacturers’ guidelines."

News.title: Family 'horrified' as they find man behind wall at Booking.com property
News.content:
Family 'horrified' as they find man behind wall at Booking.com property

A woman arranged rental accommodation to stay at with her partner and two children while they attended a family birthday - but they got the shock of their lives when they found a man behind a wall

View Image A family said they rented an entire property but found a man behind a partition (Stock) (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A woman says it was the 'most terrifying feeling ever' after her family found a man behind a wall at their rental accommodation.

‌



Therese had arranged a property to stay at with her partner and two children on Booking.com as they were attending a family birthday party.

‌



The house was close to the function and advertised as not being owner occupied, but Therese says she immediately began so suspected something wasn't quite right when the family arrived.

‌



The landlord was there with his clothes in the washing machine - but he said that he wouldn't be staying.

"I met with the landlord to get a key," Therese told Kieran Cuddihy on RTÉ’s Liveline. "That was in a key lock box. He showed me around the house. He had his clothes in his dryer at the time, and so they were drying away. I was leaving, heading back to the party, and I said, ‘Will you be here tonight when I come back?’ And he went, ‘Oh no, no, I won't be here'."

She added: "At the time I didn't realise when I booked it, the entire piece. It does have advertised the entire home is yours. But even with that regardless, I wouldn't have minded if he was staying there because B&B hosts still stay in the house sometimes. I just asked, ‘Are you going to be here tonight?’ And he went, ‘No, no, I'll be gone'."

‌



The family headed off to the party and when they returned they found another strange situation. The washing machine was running again and the key for the property was also on a chain in a lockbox outside the home. “That did make me think that he was here,” said Therese.

Feeling put off by the whole situation, Therese asked her partner to check the rooms, which is when they noticed something very strange with the property.

"Still I felt a little bit weird. So I said to my partner, ‘Will you go upstairs and just check all the rooms.' And he went up, then he came back down. He was feeling a little bit weird. We didn't initially notice that there was like this partition-looking wall," she said.

‌



"It was actually a really thin piece of plasterboard with a nail. So there was no nails on one part. This was in the sitting room, in the living room. So my partner went, ‘What's behind that?’ Because it looked like it could move. So when he went to move it, it came off.

"It was just darkness behind it and I hear ‘hey, hey’, so we obviously died. And I went, ‘Is there somebody behind that wall?’ And he went, ‘Yes’. Now the man didn't come out near us, but like straight away, I went to get the kids and just leave right now."

Therese explained she met the landlord after, who claimed to have never met her before, and told him how the experience was traumatising.

‌



"It was pitch black, so you couldn't see a thing,” Therese said. “And obviously, when you get frightened, you're not expecting to hear somebody go, ‘Hey, hey’, from a wall, which I thought was just a wall at the time.

"We left, initially had the kids outside. In the end, I did end up meeting him at the front of the house. He said that he didn't meet me before. And I said to him, ‘Why have you done this? You have traumatised myself and my kids when you easily could have just said, 'Yes, I will be here later on’.... And he went, ‘Well, my Google reviews don't say that’."

Therese said it felt like being in a "Netflix documentary". She continued: "It's horrifying. It's so scary. I genuinely. The only way to describe it is… I feel like I was on a Netflix documentary. I wouldn't believe this.

‌



"The blood drained from my face. The kids were frozen in one spot. We had to physically move them. Their jaws had dropped. They heard the hey, and all we could see was this black hole. We didn't know what size it was, whether it was a small space or big space, and we knew there was a man behind that. It's the most terrifying feeling ever."

"I’m still not over it," she said. "It's terrifying, and I feel sorry for the kids. Genuinely, will put me off booking any sort of holiday home in the future. I think I'll probably be hotels from here on in. I don't think the kids would want to stay. You just don't feel safe. Even in my own home now, it's crazy. I know I am safe, but I'm still psychologically affected by it. It's terrifying."

Booking.com confirmed a probe has been launched into the incident, and that the listing has been taken down while the investigation continues.

Article continues below

A Booking.com spokesperson told the Irish Mirror: "We take safety and security very seriously. As soon as we were made aware of this incident, we launched an investigation into the property, which is ongoing. The property has been suspended while the investigation is completed."

News.title: Mum who refused to fly for 17 years and lost boarding pass on purpose finds cure
News.content:
Mum who refused to fly for 17 years and lost boarding pass on purpose finds cure

Debbie Anderson has found a very unusual answer to her problem

View 6 Images Debbie Adamson couldn't fly for 17 years (Kennedy News and Media)

A mum was so terrified of flying she deliberately lost her boarding pass for a family holiday - only to sob when helpful airport staff gave her another. Debbie Adamson suffers from aerophobia, an intense fear of being on an aeroplane, which affects approximately one in 10 people.

‌



The retired headteacher says at its worst she once hid her boarding pass in a WHSmith magazine at Gatwick airport in a desperate attempt to avoid flying to Orlando, Florida, with her 'theme park addict' husband and three kids.

‌



The 67-year-old says she 'didn't care' even when her kids started sobbing but when airline staff simply printed her another one so she could still fly she was left 'crying solid' for three hours. Her phobia started during the 'world's worst flight' from Budapest when she was a student that left her terrified that every airplane she got on was going to crash.

‌



View 6 Images Debbie with her daughter and husband at Disneyland (Kennedy News and Media)

However, she forced herself on eight trips to Disneyland Florida with her family but says cabin crew would have to console her 'howling' and she had to hold her husband tightly. Finally she decided she 'couldn't do it' anymore and quit flying for 17 years in 2008.

‌



After learning how planes worked from a pilot pal and joining a Facebook support group, she decided to book a trip to Santorini to celebrate her 40th wedding anniversary in 2025. After learning more about her phobia, Debbie discovered that listening to a playlist of her favourite songs by Korean boyband BTS helped calm her sensory overload.

Focusing on the 'bulletproof' list of K-pop hits allowed her to fly to Orlando in Florida, US, again last year where she 'didn't bat an eyelid' even during turbulence. Now she hopes to spread awareness about her phobia to encourage others to 'give themselves permission to not be frightened'.

View 6 Images A picture taken by Debboe on a flight (Kennedy News and Media)

‌



Debbie, from Southampton, Hampshire, said: "When I was a student I flew to Budapest and we had the world's worst flight, it was my first flight and I was on my own. When we landed it bounced down the wrong way and there were sparks coming off the wing tips and it was lurching. It was your horror come true.

"From that point onwards I thought every aeroplane I ever got on was going to crash. It was shocking and it was horrible. After that I didn't want to go anywhere on a plane ever again, I was terrified. I then went and married a theme park addict and I made myself go on those flights for my family. It was the flight crew that was my coping strategy.

‌



"When I had to fly during this terrified period, I would tell the stewardess [about my phobia] when I went through the door if I wasn't [already] crying. My husband used to come off every flight with permanent arthritis in his hands where I'd be holding onto him so tightly.

View 6 Images A picture taken by Debboe on a flight (Kennedy News and Media)

‌



"I can't explain it, you just can't control it. It's just abject terror, it's ridiculous. Even the slightest hint of turbulence I'd be crying again if I stopped. I never ate or drank, I came off flights feeling quite unwell. It was really quite bad.

"One time I was sitting at the airport and said 'I need to go into the bathroom'. I veered into WH Smith and I had my boarding pass with me and I put it in a girly magazine where I thought no one would ever look on the top shelf.

"I came weeping back saying 'I've lost my boarding pass, I can't go'. My kids all started crying. We got to an airline representative and said 'can you help, she's lost her boarding pass?'. There I was thinking they'd say 'she's got to go home' but they printed me another one.

‌



"I cried solid for at least three hours. I got onto that plane with dehydration I cried so much. I still did it though, it never got worse than that."

View 6 Images Debbie and her family in the USA (Kennedy News and Media)

‌



Debbie revealed that she started learning how planes worked from her pilot pal and joined a Facebook support group to learn more about overcoming her phobia. After 17 years of refusing to fly she decided to book a trip to Santorini where she says she discovered that listening to her favourite boyband BTS helped to calm her sensory overload.

Debbie said: "I'd always wanted to go to Santorini but I thought 'can I even face it?' My partner was pleasantly surprised when I suggested the Santorini trip. If I could pinpoint one thing, taking out the sensory overload was what changed it. I sat there with every sense bombarding me with distressing information.

"So I thought I'd take two out and I made a bulletproof playlist - every single track I love so that I knew I'd keep listening. I shut my eyes during take-off and I also held on very tightly too, once I did that I began to rationalise it.

‌



"It just proved to myself that I gave myself permission not to be frightened anymore so I wasn't. All the pressure was put on me by my own mind. On the way back from the trip to Orlando the pilot said it was going to be a bumpy flight and it was and I didn't bat an eyelid.

View 6 Images Debbie and her family boarding a flight (Kennedy News and Media)

‌



"Just as the first big bump came Bruce Springsteen started playing on the movie I was just watching and it was 'Born in the USA'. The plane went 'boom' and I just laughed. I'm completely different. [I was] bouncing along to the Bruce Springsteen film whereas before I would've been crying my head off with stewardesses on either side of me trying to calm me down.

"It can be quite disarming when someone's howling."

Now Debbie says she is looking to book more trips in the future and hopes to spread awareness about her experience to help others living with the phobia. Debbie said: "I'd never say I'm cured but having that self-awareness to think 'I'm going to take out those three senses and I'm going to give myself permission to not be frightened'.

Article continues below

"It wasn't anything to be ashamed of, I couldn't help it, but what I hadn't done was to allow my mind the freedom to find out about this and be a bit more logical about this. It's understandable to feel like that but you don't have to and you can choose not to. It sounds so easy but it's so hard to do. I feel changed. It opens up a whole new vista."

News.title: Woman dies as man falls from 12-storey building and lands on her – but he survives
News.content:
Woman dies as man falls from 12-storey building and lands on her – but he survives

Emergency services were called to reports that 'a man fell and hit a woman' in Nagoya City, Japan - the woman died but the man has survived

View 2 Images The apartment blocks where the man fell (Image: Unsplash)

A 23-year-old woman has tragically died in Japan after a man plunged onto her from a 12-storey block of flats. He survived the fall.

‌



Emergency services were called to a report that "a man fell and hit a woman" in Naka-ku, Nagoya City at around 1am on July 19.

‌



Police named the victim as Tomohiro Inaba, who was a shop assistant working nearby. She was taken to the hospital where she was sadly pronounced dead several hours later from haemorrhagic shock.

‌



It is understood she had been walking on a path under the window where Nobushige Taguchi, 29, also a shop worker, fell and landed on top of her. He survived the fall but is fighting for his life in hospital having sustained severe head and chest injuries, and is in a coma.

View 2 Images The woman was taken to hospital but tragically died (stock) (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The incident took place around 500m northeast of Yabamachi Station on the Nagoya Municipal Subway Meijo Line, in an area densely populated with high-rise buildings and apartments, reports Kyodo News.

‌



The person who alerted police was a friend of the victim who was walking alongside her but suffered no injuries. Other people also rushed to the scene in the early hours of the morning after hearing screams.

An investigation is now underway into how the man came to fall and police are looking into whether he jumped or if it is an accident.

The area was cordoned off following the incident with forensic officers gathering evidence from the scene, although it is unclear from which floor of the apartment block the man fell.

‌



Local media reports the man was not a resident living in the block of flats and so part of the investigation will also look into why he was there.

It comes after a woman was killed after a pensioner jumped from a fourth-floor apartment in Milan last September - he also survived the fall.

Francesca Manno, 83, died after walking under the balcony of the building in the Baggio district of the city when she was hit by a 70-year-old man who fell directly on top of her.

Article continues below

The man had climbed over his balcony railing in the building where both he and Ms Manno lived, according to Corriere Milano.

Police initially believed it had been a double suicide attempt but then an investigation found that the two were strangers and Ms Manno's death had been a tragic accident.

For mental health support, contact the Samaritans on 116 123, email them at jo@samaritans.org or visit samaritans.org to find your nearest branch.

News.title: Police have last laugh after 'ab-tastic' fugitive who shared alternate mugshot gets caught
News.content:
Police have last laugh after 'ab-tastic' fugitive who shared alternate mugshot gets caught

A man wanted on recall to prison posted a boasting topless selfie in response to a police appeal for his arrest on social media. But it seems like officers were the ones with the last laugh

View 2 Images Nathan Muir's mug shot left, and a topless selfie posted in the comments of a GMP Facebook post (Image: GMP/Facebook/M.E.N.)

A fugitive who mocked police on social media has had justice catch up to him, with the Manchester man sharing a far more flattering image of himself in response to a social media appeal calling on the public to help track him down.

‌



Last month, Greater Manchester Police' s Wythenshawe division shared a public appeal via Facebook, calling on locals to let them know as they continued to hunt for 32-year-old Nathan Muir, who was on the lam.

‌



It would seem that Muir was less than impressed by the mugshot shared by police, logging on to Facebook himself to share an alternative image in the comments section. Alongside the image, which featured so many abs in it it should be deemed criminal, Muir - who was still at large - wrote: "Could of done a better pic (sic)."

‌



The photo appears to have been taken during his time behind bars. But now it would seem that the prison gym has got back its star member, with officers eventually catching up to him. He has since been returned to prison.

The initial appeal sought help in finding Muir, who reportedly had connections to Wythenshawe, Hale and Altrincham but no fixed abode, as he was wanted 'on recall to prison', reports the Manchester Evening News.

View 2 Images Nathan Muir's mug shot left, and a topless selfie posted in the comments of a GMP Facebook post (Image: GMP/Facebook/M.E.N.)

‌



The post, featuring Muir's mug shot, read: "#WANTED | Police are appealing for the public's help to find a wanted man from Greater Manchester. Nathan Muir (23/09/1994) of no fixed abode, is wanted on recall to prison.

"He is believed to have links to #Wythenshawe, #Hale and #Altrincham. Any info? Please contact 101 or 0161 856 1748 with information regarding his whereabouts."

Shortly after, a Facebook profile under the name 'Nay Muir' posted a shirtless selfie in the comments, captioned: "Could of done a better pic [sic]."

‌



The image received 'likes' from hundreds of people. This was followed by AI-generated images of Muir enjoying a pint and sunbathing outside Wythenshawe police station.

Today, GMP Wythenshawe shared an update about the case on its Facebook page, featuring another decidedly untoned picture of Muir.

‌



The post stated: "While his famous abs appear to have escaped justice, he didn't.

"Remember Nathan Muir who wanted a "better pic" on his recall to prison appeal? Good news, Muir was arrested this morning at an address in #Stockport following extensive enquiries and has been sent back to prison.

"We'd like to thank those who shared our appeal."

Article continues below

Users supported the police's approach, with one commenting that Muir had been 'trolled by the feds'.

News.title: B&M hit with huge fine as mouse infestation and droppings found in UK stores
News.content:
B&M hit with huge fine as mouse infestation and droppings found in UK stores

B&M Retail Ltd admitted the offences in Magistrates Court, and has been fined £2 million after members of the public made complaints about the stores in question to health authorities

View 3 Images File photo of a B&M store sign (Image: Getty Images)

Discount food, garden, and homeware superstore B&M Retail Ltd has been fined £2 million over food hygiene offences found at three stores.

‌



Inspectors discovered a m ouse infestation, droppings, and gnawed food products at three stores in Birmingham after public complaints were made to the council's environmental health team between November 2024 and October 2025. After probing stores at St Andrews Retail Park, Priory Square Shopping Centre, and The Fort Shopping Park, B&M pleaded guilty.

‌



The business admitted offences in Magistrates' Court and was sentenced on July 13, reports Birmingham Live.

‌



The council said that inspectors visited the store at St Andrews Retail Park on November 11, 2024 following reports of pests on the premises.

View 3 Images Some B&M stores also feature a garden centre range (Image: Nigel A Messenger via Getty Images)

Officers found significant evidence of mouse activity, including mouse droppings and gnawed food products on sale, the council said. Due to the serious risk to public health, a Hygiene Emergency Prohibition Notice was served.

‌



An inspection was carried out at the B&M at Priory Square Shopping Centre store after receiving a complaint from a member of the public who reported seeing a mouse in the shop.

During the visit, officers found evidence of an active mouse infestation, including gnawed food products, mouse droppings and urine contamination on food packaging and shelving, inadequate cleaning standards and structural defects allowing pest entry on January 22, last year, the council said.

A Hygiene Emergency Prohibition Notice was served and the store was closed immediately.

‌



And a further inspection took place at B&M's store at The Fort Shopping Park on October 27, last year, following a complaint alleging a mouse infestation.

Officers found widespread evidence of mouse activity throughout the premises, including mouse droppings and gnawed food products on the shop floor and within storage areas, the council said.

View 3 Images (Image: Google)

‌



Mouse droppings were also found in proximity to children's toys on display. Owing to the risks posed to public health, the premises was formally closed using another Hygiene Emergency Prohibition Notice.

B&M Retail Ltd pleaded guilty to the offences at Birmingham Magistrates' Court. A sentencing hearing took place on July 13.

The company was ordered to pay a £2m fine, prosecution costs of £18,104, and a victim surcharge of £2,000 - each payable within 28 days.

Article continues below

Speaking after the case, Cllr Sam Forsyth, Chair of the Licensing and Public Protection Committee, said: "Residents rightly expect businesses operating in Birmingham to maintain high standards and provide safe environments for customers. The health and wellbeing of Birmingham residents will always come first, and the conditions identified by our Environmental Health officers across these stores were unacceptable and required immediate intervention to protect the public.

“I welcome the work of our Environmental Health teams in identifying these risks and taking swift action. This substantial court penalty reflects the seriousness of the offences and sends a clear message that businesses must take their responsibilities seriously. Birmingham City Council will continue to take robust enforcement action where necessary to protect residents and ensure standards are upheld across the city."

News.title: Pensioner, 70, arrested over 'bladed article' after incident on Welsh beach
News.content:
Pensioner, 70, arrested over 'bladed article' after incident on Welsh beach

A 70-year-old man was arrested on Aberavon Beach in Wales after officers from South Wales Police attended following reports of anti-social behaviour

View Image The man was arrested on Aberavon Beach (file image) (Image: John Myers)

A pensioner has been arrested following an incident on a popular beach in Wales.

Police were called to Aberavon Beach at around 1.40pm on Monday following reports of anti-social behaviour.

Officers from South Wales Police attended the beach and arrested a 70-year-old man, who police said was found to be in breach of police bail conditions. He remains in custody, Wales Online reports.

A South Wales Police spokesperson said: "Officers attended Aberavon beachfront at around 1.40pm yesterday (Monday, July 20) following a report of anti-social behaviour.

"Upon arrival the man concerned was identified to be subject to police bail conditions of which he was in breach.

Article continues below

"The man - 70 years old and from Birmingham - was also arrested on suspicion of possession of a bladed article. He is currently in police custody."

News.title: Princess Charlotte's subtle gestures in public 'always makes Prince George fall in line'
News.content:
Princess Charlotte's subtle gestures in public 'always makes Prince George fall in line'

A body language expert, along with other royal voices, have spoken in a Channel 5 documentary about the relationship between Prince George and his sister Princess Charlotte

View 3 Images Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis during Trooping The Colour (Image: Getty Images)

Prince George is often kept “in line” by his younger sister Princess Charlotte who makes subtle gestures during public royal events, according to a body language expert.

‌



The future monarch turns 13 years old today and the now teenager is said to share a close bond with his siblings Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight.

‌



And Judi James, who has studied their body languages on different occasions, has noticed a trend when it comes to Charlotte and her two brothers.

‌



She spoke about it in a Channel 5 documentary called Prince George at 13: The Next Generation — where royal author Katie Nicholl also gave a similar insight.

Katie said: “I think he [George] rather depends on Charlotte and certainly did in the early days when it came to their public engagements and walkabouts when George could seem, I think compared to his sister, quite shy.”

View 3 Images The family pictured on the balcony of Buckingham Palace following the Platinum Pageant in 2022 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Royal expert Ingrid Sward then revealed Charlotte “tells him what to do” before Katie added: “I think we very much saw that when they did their first Trooping The Colour and you had all three children in that carriage and it was very much Charlotte keeping Louis in check, making sure George was ok.”

Body language expert Judi then gave her own take about what she has observed from the royal children in recent years.

She said: “We do see Charlotte keeping an eye on both of her brothers. What I found really fascinating isn’t so much that she is doing that, but for me, it is the way that when she does nudge them and tap them, they both fall into line.

‌



“Children of that age, normally if a younger sibling says put your arms down, [they’ll reply] ‘who do you think you are?’

“But they absolutely take it and I think that’s going to be very important when it comes to the dynamic because they will see that as a form of support.”

View 3 Images Prince William and Princess Kate with their three children (Image: Getty Images)

‌



She added: “I think that in terms of the relationship it probably would compare a little bit to Anne and Charles where Anne was always the more confident sibling and I think Charlotte to a certain extent she seems to absolutely get protocol. She knows what needs to be done.

“I don’t think either of them [George or Louis] have got hugely strong attention spams, they will be watching the planes or talking about something. So I think that helps them relax a little bit because they know that if they are doing anything wrong, they have got their sister there, who is usually in the middle of them.

“So in a way, I think it’s probably she goes out being the keeper of the choreography so they don’t have to, but at the same time, they know that if they do anything wrong, she will be there to correct them.”

Article continues below

As of September, George will no longer attend the same preparatory school in Berkshire as his siblings, and will follow in his father’s footsteps by going to Eton.

And as he celebrates starting his teenage years, his dad Prince William is reportedly “thrilled” that his eldest son will attend Eton for his secondary school education.

Prince George at 13: The Next Generation will air on Channel 5 on Saturday (July 25) at 9pm

News.title: Chris Mason: Another Starmer critic gets promotion as Sarwar joins Burnham government
News.content:
The imminent appointment of the Scottish Labour leader Anas Sarwar to Andy Burnham's government, via a seat in the House of Lords, sees the promotion of another key figure in the downfall of Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister.

When Sarwar said publicly, back in February, that Sir Keir should stand down, it was a moment of colossal jeopardy for the now former prime minister.

It looked, briefly, like it might bring about an immediate and irrevocable collapse in his authority. Then, one after another, cabinet ministers posted their support for him on social media.

As I wrote at the time, missives of public loyalty from cabinet ministers towards a prime minister shouldn't be newsworthy and they only become so when the opposite seems feasible.

Now, five months on, Sarwar will be swapping Holyrood for Westminster and becoming a minister.

He will be joining Miatta Fahnbulleh in government, the new energy secretary in Burnham's cabinet, who was the first government minister to resign from Sir Keir's administration saying she had lost faith in him.

Also around the cabinet table, the new Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who let it be known in what turned out to be Sir Keir's final weeks in office that he had suggested to him that he ought to accept that his time was up.

It is also worth mentioning too John Healey, who resigned as defence secretary, and Wes Streeting, who resigned as health secretary towards the end of Sir Keir's time in Downing Street, are now in prominent roles in Burnham's cabinet as chancellor and defence secretary respectively.

This is the backdrop to comments from Steve Reed, the former communities secretary and doughty defender of Sir Keir at some of his moments of most intense peril.

Reed wrote to Burnham as he left government and said: "I hope those who did not show loyalty to Keir will now show it to you. I am proud that I acted with integrity at every step over the turbulent past few months."

There is, right now, as you would expect, overwhelming support for Burnham among Labour MPs.

But these public remarks from Reed are an indicator of the wells of private hurt and anger created by the events of recent days, weeks and months.

It is a reminder that, of course, all the folk you are reading and hearing about are human beings who have each keenly felt the tremors of uncertainty in recent months â and depending on their circumstances, outlook, instincts and judgement, have arrived at differing conclusions and decisions about how to act.

The public intervention of Darren Jones, another loyal lieutenant of the former prime minister, taking a swipe at the funding of the government's planned cut in VAT on domestic electricity bills should be seen in this context too.

Labour's switch from one leader to another was less drawn out and dramatic than it might have been, as there was neither a formal leadership challenge to Sir Keir, nor more than one contender to replace him once he had announced his intention to go.

But it is also true that what we have witnessed the climax of this week, and the build up to for months on end, is not cost or pain free for a political party and some of that is manifesting itself now â and may still do for some time.

News.title: PC Harper killers' potential early release is an 'insult', says his mother
News.content:
The mother of police officer Andrew Harper has said it feels like an "insult" that two of her son's killers may be eligible for early release from prison.

PC Harper was 28 years old when he sustained fatal injuries while responding to a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in August 2019.

He died after getting caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and dragged down a country road as three teenage suspects fled the scene of the burglary.

Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were passengers in the car and both 17 at the time, were handed 13 years in custody for manslaughter after a trial at the Old Bailey in 2020.

Both men might be eligible to be released from prison halfway through their sentences, the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) has confirmed.

Under the new Sentencing Act, due to come into force in September, some 6,000 criminals are set to be released under the early prison release scheme.

The government has so far failed to rule out whether killers, rapists and paedophiles will be exempt from the scheme.

The driver of the vehicle which caused PC Harper's death, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence, and will not be eligible for the scheme.

News.title: More women in their 20s are getting type 2 diabetes, experts warn
News.content:
England is seeing a "worrying increase" in young women in their 20s developing type 2 diabetes, experts at Imperial College London have warned.

The rise has largely occurred since the Covid pandemic and is closely linked to increasing obesity levels, according to an analysis of NHS data from 2011 to 2024, external.

Type 2 diabetes is serious, and can lead to severe complications, such as heart attacks and strokes.

When it develops at a younger age, the disease tends to be more aggressive, raising the risk of devastating complications and cutting lives short, according to Diabetes UK.

News.title: Military kit still failing women, troops say
News.content:
Women in the armed forces say they are still being issued kit that does not fit properly, five years after a landmark report warned they were at "greater risk of harm" from ill-fitting uniform and equipment.

The 2021 Atherton report said the Ministry of Defence should urgently roll out safer, more appropriate kit for female service personnel by the end of 2022.

Despite improvements, women have been telling the BBC some kit is still poorly fitting, with body armour failing to account for breasts, and shortages of smaller sizes resulting in "competition" among troops.

The Ministry of Defence (MOD) said it ensured everyone had access to the "best equipment they need to protect themselves in combat".

"I never felt that I was neat, tidy, presentable, or in the uniform that I was meant to be in," explains veteran Rhian Brown, who left the service in 2024.

"I never really felt that it protected me or entirely fulfilled the purpose that it was meant to."

News.title: Nottingham attacks NHS trust faces manslaughter probe
News.content:
The NHS trust that treated Nottingham attacks killer Valdo Calocane is being investigated for corporate manslaughter.

Calocane, who had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia before he fatally attacked Barnaby Webber, Grace O'Malley-Kumar and Ian Coates in June 2023, was previously sectioned by Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust.

A public inquiry, which finished hearing evidence in May, was told he had been discharged in 2022 because he failed to turn up for appointments and the team had "lost" him.

The investigation into the trust is being carried out by Northumbria Police.

Nottinghamshire Police has been criticised over its history of interactions with Calocane and its handling of the response and investigation into the attacks.

A spokesperson for Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust said: "Northumbria Police, acting on behalf of Nottinghamshire Police, have begun an investigation into matters relating to the care and treatment of Valdo Calocane.

"We know how important the independent inquiry and police investigation are for the affected families, the survivors and our local communities.

"We will, of course, be co-operating fully with Northumbria Police, as we have with the Statutory Inquiry into these matters which is being chaired by Her Honour Deborah Taylor, and which will hear final submissions from all the parties involved later this year."

News.title: Streeting apologises after early prisoner release comments heard on mic
News.content:
Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has said there was "no ill intent" behind comments he made apparently about the early prisoner release scheme, which were caught on camera.

In a video, published by the news website Guido Fawkes, the new Justice Secretary Alex Norris can be seen walking towards Streeting and Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood.

Streeting, can then be heard calling Norris "the enemy now" while Mahmood responds "no he's not". Streeting goes on to say "he wants to let them all out" - appearing to reference the government's plans for early release for prisoners.

The comments have been criticised by Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch for making light of the scheme, which her party opposes.

"While Andy Burnham's cabinet are joking about letting criminals out of prison early, Conservatives are listening to victims and will continue to fight this disgusting policy," the Conservative leader wrote on X.

Streeting and the home secretary, Mahmood, have both apologised for the comments caught on the hot mic with both labelling the early release scheme a "serious issue".

"I hope everyone can see there was no ill intent behind this ribbing of the new justice secretary - it was a reference to an old May/Clarke joke," the defence secretary said in a post on X.

"But I appreciate these are very serious issues and am sorry for any offence inadvertently caused by this moment of levity."

In 2017, Theresa May said of her Conservative colleague Ken Clarke, who had served as justice secretary, that: "When I was home secretary, I used to say 'I locked 'em up and he let 'em out'."

The home secretary wrote: "I think everyone can see there was no ill intent behind this ribbing of the new Lord Chancellor - a role I once filled and which comes with immense challenges thanks to the vandalism inflicted on our justice system by the last Conservative government.

"But I appreciate this is an extremely serious issue and do not want anyone to mistake this moment of levity for a lack of serious intent."

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said it was "right" that Streeting had apologised.

"Those remarks don't reflect the seriousness with which all of them will approach matters relating to public safety and the prison system."

Shortly after coming to power in 2024, the Labour government announced emergency measures to release prisoners early in a bid to ease overcrowding in prisons.

At one point, the Prison Governors' Association had warned that jails were due to run out of space within days.

Alexander defended the government's actions, saying: "Difficult but necessary decisions had to be taken to ensure the prison system could continue functioning.

"We were in danger of a situation where the courts couldn't sentence because there weren't prison spaces available and police wouldn't be able to make arrests."

News.title: Great Apes kiss and cuddle to keep the peace, says study
News.content:
Touching, embracing and kissing before stressful events may be an ancient way of building trust, according to scientists studying the behaviour of our closest ape relatives.

Researchers at Durham University studied chimpanzees and bonobos using physical contact to reassure each other ahead of conflicts over food.

One of the most surprising findings was that chimpanzees, despite their reputation for aggression, engaged in close contact, including placing fingers in one another's mouths.

"Before stressful events, they come together, they reassure each other, they touch each other, they hug each other," said Prof Zanna Clay.

News.title: I've got a motorway in my garden - it's my shelter in hot weather
News.content:
Narelle Cowan and Aimee Lipley's gardens have a few things in common.

Both have pretty plants, chairs for al fresco dining - and one of the UK's busiest motorways.

About 75,000 vehicles travel over the elevated concrete monolith hanging about 45ft (14m) above their plot every day on the main route between London and south Wales.

"I call it my free gazebo," said Aimee. "I love it under here, when it's raining you can walk to the shops without getting your hair wet."

The two-lane carriageway in the sky was one of the first sections of the M4 and a relic of the 1960s freeway building boom after the explosion in post-war car ownership.

News.title: PM tells cabinet to tackle living costs at first meeting
News.content:
Andy Burnham has promised to lead a "cost of living government," as he chaired his first cabinet meeting as prime minister.

He told his newly assembled top team that he wanted to make living expenses a key priority, and give people a "sense that help is coming" on costs.

It comes after he announced a VAT cut to household energy bills from October, in his first major announcement since taking office.

But his plan to pay for the policy by scrapping Sir Keir Starmer's digital ID scheme led to an early row over whether the plan was properly funded.

Downing Street said the estimated Â£850m cost of the VAT cut over the rest of the financial year could come from Â£1.8bn earmarked by the previous government to roll out the digital ID scheme in the next three years.

But Darren Jones, who was among a clutch of Starmer loyalists sacked from the cabinet on Monday, said the ID programme was "unfunded" and Burnham would need to set out where the money would be found.

Opposition parties also seized on the announcement, pointing out the government's budget watchdog has previously said the money to fund digital ID was due to be found from within existing budgets.

"We are only one day in and already Labour are playing fast and loose with the public finances," said Conservative shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride.

The PM's spokesman insisted the policy would be funded by redirecting "savings" identified by departments to cover the cost of the ID scheme.

News.title: Ann Widdecombe was hit on head 21 times with hammer, prosecutors say
News.content:
Ann Widdecombe was hit on the head with a hammer 21 times at her home as she ate lunch in an attack that was caught on camera, prosecutors have told Westminster Magistrates' Court.

Prosecutor Kashif Malik said the man charged with her murder, Joshua Kerry, arrived at her house on 8 July in a red Vauxhall Corsa and entered through the front door.

Kerry, who prosecutors say was in the property for two minutes and was wearing black gloves, then allegedly hit Widdecombe repeatedly with a hammer in her kitchen, tipped her from her chair and took her wallet before driving off.

The 28-year-old from South Yorkshire later also appeared at the Old Bailey and was remanded in custody.

At the Old Bailey hearing, prosecutor Alistair Richardson said the attack on Widdecombe had been carried out with a "ferocity of violence".

Malik told the court that Widdecombe did not attend a pre-arranged online interview with Channel 5's Matt Allwright show that had been scheduled for just before 13:00 BST on 8 July.

The show's production team tried to contact Widdecombe through her personal assistant, who then asked Widdecombe's gardener to check on her, the court heard.

Prosecutors said the gardener entered the house via the open front door on 9 July and found Widdecombe lying face down on her kitchen floor with a serious head injury.

News.title: UK humanitarian worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital
News.content:
A humanitarian worker in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been medically evacuated to the UK after a potential healthcareârelated exposure to Ebola.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said the individual, who is a UK resident and has not been named, has no symptoms, and the move is purely precautionary.

The individual remains well but is being assessed and monitored at a London hospital, the statement from UKHSA said.

The hospital has not been named but the Royal Free in north London has a high level isolation unit and is the primary national centre for high consequence infectious diseases.

The incubation period of Ebola ranges from two to 21 days and the humanitarian worker will be required to isolate throughout.

The individual had been working with a humanitarian organisation supporting the Ebola outbreak response.

Ebola is a highly dangerous pathogen. Unlike flu or Covid, it is not airborne and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids.

Symptoms come on suddenly and start like the flu or malaria, with fever, headache and tiredness. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

Richard Pebody, director of epidemic and emerging infections at UKHSA, said: "The risk to the general public remains low.

"This individual has been transferred out of an abundance of caution, and we're pleased they remain well."

There are currently no confirmed cases of Ebola in the UK, the agency said.

News.title: 'My sister is not just another statistic'  - Jennie's Law is signed
News.content:
Jennifer Poole, a woman murdered by her former partner, will not be "another statistic" her brother has said after a new law in her name was signed off in the Republic of Ireland.

Jason Poole's sister was unaware her partner Gavin Murphy had a history of domestic violence when he murdered her in her Dublin home in 2021.

The Domestic Violence (Judgements) Register Bill 2026, external, known as Jennie's Law, was approved by the DÃ¡il (Irish parliament) and has now been signed off by Irish President Catherine Connolly.

It will result in those convicted of domestic violence against a partner being included on a public register.

News.title: 'We just need a bed' - Baby with 'days to live' can't access lifesaving treatment
News.content:
The parents of a three-month-old boy who they fear has just days to live say they're frustrated at being unable to access lifesaving treatment due to a lack of suitable hospital beds.

Dylan and Catrin Green, from Cardiff, said their "completely healthy baby" Macs started to struggle with his feeding, then caught a cold before later suffering two cardiac arrests.

He has been diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy, external - a condition which can lead to heart failure - and now has a "matter of days" on a machine which pumps his heart for him, Dylan said.

He urgently needs a Berlin heart , external- a device used to take over the function of a child's own heart until a donor heart becomes available.

His family said Macs has been stuck at a specialist unit in Bristol for weeks, where his condition has since deteriorated and was now in an induced coma, as the beds he needs were not available.

The two specialist hospitals in the UK where the Berlin heart can be fitted are Great Ormond Street Hospital in London and the Freeman Hospital in Newcastle.

News.title: Parts of the UK move closer to drought
News.content:
Summer so far has been exceptionally hot and dry across much of the UK, with three widespread heatwaves and the longest run of dry days in central England since 1995. England, Wales and eastern Scotland have been the driest areas over recent weeks, and this follows a very dry spring in similar regions.

England has received only 3% of its long-term average July rainfall with the south and east of England seeing no rain at all. Wisley in Surrey has seen 33 consecutive dry days.

Rainfall so far this summer has been below average across the UK as a whole, but there has been large regional contrast.

Up to the middle of summer - 15 July - parts of eastern and north-eastern England had received just 26% of their total expected summer rainfall. Areas of northern and western Scotland had more than average for the first half of the summer, though.

In Wales, where just 5% of July rainfall has fallen, Natural Resources Wales has moved the worst affected regions in the north and south-east into "prolonged dry weather status", the first step in its drought plan.

Comparisons are being made with last summer, when drought was declared across much of England, Wales and eastern Scotland. It officially ended just four months ago.

This year, drought has not developed as quickly because heavy rainfall recharged our aquifers, rivers and reservoirs during a very wet autumn and winter.

However, the UK Centre for Ecology and Hydrology says flash droughts, external with a sudden transition between wet and dry conditions are "likely to happen more often, and be more intense".

As the effects of human-induced climate change continue, the Met Office expects our summers to become hotter and drier, external in the future. In fact, by 2070, our summers could be up to 60% drier and 1-6C warmer compared to 1990.

News.title: Russian warship carried out firing exercise off Plymouth coast
News.content:
The live-fire exercise took place in international waters and lasted for 30 minutes.

The Russian warship requested that the Royal Navy's HMS Tyne reposition to a safer distance, which it did.

The Russian frigate was also being monitored by a French military aircraft which made radio contact with the warship asking it to clarify its intentions, the BBC has been told.

BBC Verify has analysed flight and ship-tracking data which shows the position of HMS Tyne and several British military aircraft operating in and around the Channel near Plymouth on Monday.

Flight data on ADS-B Exchange indicates at least four Royal Air Force and Royal Navy aircraft were flying off the coast of Dorset mostly above the UK's territorial waters, including two Eurofighter Typhoons, a Voyager air refuelling tanker and a Super Lynx helicopter.

A French military H160M GuÃ©pard helicopter also flew out and over the Channel during the afternoon. It is not clear if this is the aircraft which made contact with the Russian warship.

Data on ship-tracking service MarineTraffic shows HMS Tyne began to broadcast its location about 40 miles off Plymouth at 13:57 BST on Monday. It remained in that location for around two hours before departing at 15:56 to return to Plymouth.

HMS Tyne has been tracking Neustrashimy since at least 16 July when both vessels were also captured in the North Sea about 36 miles miles from the port of Felixstowe in Suffolk on a satellite image.

The incident will be a reminder for the new prime minister of increased Russian naval activity near UK waters in recent months.

Last month, Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in a six-hour operation which was the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

Also in June, a British couple in international waters in the English Channel came across a Russian warship - Admiral Grigorovich - 23 miles off the Isle of Wight.

The frigate fired warning shots as Jane and Alan Kelvey sailed their yacht on what Russia's defence ministry said had been a "dangerous approach". However, the couple said they had not been on a "collision course".

Russian warships regularly pass through international waters in the Channel, which are separate from UK and French territorial waters.

News.title: Boy, 15, accused of sex attacks on eight girls
News.content:
A 15-year-old boy charged with sexual offences against eight girls, including one who was 10 years old, has appeared in court.

The complainants were aged between 10 and 15 at the time, Wellingborough Youth Court heard.

The teenager, who cannot be named because of his age, faces 22 charges relating to alleged incidents between 2023 and 2025, including rape.

He was not asked to enter any pleas during a 20-minute hearing, before the case was sent to Northampton Crown Court for 18 August.

The defendant, who was accompanied by his mother, was released on bail.

Details of where the offences took place have been withheld to protect the alleged victims' right to anonymity.

The boy has been charged with:

Twelve counts of sexually assaulting a female

Three offences of assaulting a girl under 13 by touching

Two counts of rape and a further two of making an indecent photograph or pseudo-photograph of a child

Assaulting a female by penetration

Possessing a prohibited image of a child and possessing an extreme pornographic image or images

District Judge Amar Mehta told the boy: "Your case is too serious to be tried in this court."

His bail conditions included not to contact the alleged victims and to have no unsupervised contact with females under 16.

The boy spoke only to confirm his name, date of birth and address. He also asked the judge to explain what the Youth Justice Service was.
