Sports.title: Could the World Cup be back in the US as soon as 2038? Absolutely
Sports.content:
As is often the case, it has been left to Donald Trump to say the quiet bit out loud. “We have to do this again and we have to do it while I’m around, you hear that Gianni?” the US president told Fox News in an interview broadcast in the buildup to the World Cup final.

An American bid for the 2038 World Cup has been the talk of the hotel lobbies populated by administrators from around the world over the past month, who have watched this country’s seemingly limitless appetite for major events and willingness to pay whatever it takes to attend them.

Fifa has been quietly, but actively encouraging a US bid for some time and in a meeting at the Waldorf Astoria on Park Avenue in New York on Saturday it became clearer why.

The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, told representatives of the governing body’s 211 member associations that its revenue projections for the current four-year cycle has increased from $11bn (£8.2bn) to $15bn, with the vast majority of the growth coming from an explosion in ticketing and hospitality revenue.

A Fifa source disclosed that such has been the demand in the US in particular that ticketing and hospitality sales have gone past $5bn, with that part of the market now worth more than the World Cup’s TV rights for the first time.

“Fifa will want to get back here as quickly as possible,” said a senior figure at one of its hospitality partners.

While ticket sales have exceeded expectations, helped by the dynamic pricing and secondary market resale models that are embedded in US culture, in one crucial respect Fifa left a huge amount of money on the table, another reason it is desperate to return.

In an extraordinary deal, Fox Sports was awarded English-language TV rights in the US by Fifa without a bidding process, a precautionary move by the world governing body to prevent a lawsuit when Qatar 2022 was moved to the winter after the TV contracts had already been signed, creating a direct clash with the US domestic sports season, particularly the NFL and NBA.

With no competitive tension, Fox was given a relative bargain, paying $485m for the 2026 rights, the same as in Qatar, despite the World Cup having an extra 40 matches and taking place on home soil. For context, the NFL’s domestic TV deal is worth $11bn a year, with the NBA bringing in around $7bn.

Fox has capitalised this summer as a result, on the back of bumper viewing, with industry experts predicting it will make more than $1bn from TV adverts, whose volume and value has increased due to the addition of hydration breaks.

Fifa is determined to recoup what many regard as lost income from the US market in future TV rights cycles.

Having watched with frustration as Fox has cashed in, ESPN and NBC are expected to bid for the 2030 tournament, while initial conversations have also taken place with Netflix about them joining in the auction.

View image in fullscreen High prices did not deter fans from packing out stadiums at the World Cup in the US. Photograph: Julio Cortez/AP

Netflix has already signalled its growing interest in football by buying American rights for the Women’s World Cup in 2027 and 2031, the latter being held in the US, and another men’s tournament seven years later would spark another boom.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No country has hosted the World Cup twice in 12 years, but Fifa’s statutes and recent staging decisions give it the flexibility for this to happen.

By taking the 2030 World Cup to three continents and six countries – Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay – before Saudi Arabia hosts in 2034, a North American bid for 2038 is permitted under Fifa’s confederation rotation policy, along with one from Oceania.

Soccer Australia had wanted to bid for 2034, but after being given less than a month to formally register its interest by Fifa, withdrew its candidacy leaving Saudi Arabia to be selected unopposed, Infantino’s preferred method.

To complicate matters slightly, the North American confederation, Concacaf, is understood to have reservations about another US bid as it wants to give opportunities to other members.

Costa Rica, Jamaica and Mexico have been added to the 2031 Women’s World Cup bid and another joint endeavour could emerge, although unsurprisingly Trump would prefer the US to be sole hosts. “Based on the numbers we will be requesting it again immediately,” he told Fox.

Fifa’s timeline for opening the 2038 process is not yet known, but history suggests it could move quickly to secure the outcome it wants. The sudden opening of the 2034 bidding process in October 2024 took most confederations by surprise with Infantino announcing that Saudi Arabia would be the hosts just 25 days later, a decision ratified by all Fifa members at a bizarre virtual extraordinary general meeting two months later.

Infantino will be re-elected for a fourth full term at next year’s Fifa Congress in Morocco, almost certainly unopposed, and then all eyes will turn to the 2038 contest.

Barring what would be an unprecedented change to the US constitution to permit an additional term, Trump is due to leave office in January 2029, which may quickly become the deadline for Fifa.

Sports.title: Liverpool owner FSG in talks over selling 30% stake to Bhatia consortium for £1.35bn
Sports.content:
Liverpool’s owner is in talks over ­selling a minority stake to a consortium led by the former Queens Park Rangers co‑owner Amit ­Bhatia and backed by his father-in-law ­Lakshmi Mittal, the billionaire Indian steel magnate. The Guardian understands a sale of 30% of the club is being discussed, with an offer of around £1.35bn on the table.

Fenway Sports Group confirmed in a statement to the Financial Times that it had begun negotiations with a group led by Bhatia over a ­potential minority share sale that would value ­Liverpool at about £4.5bn.

“An investment consortium led and ­managed by Amit Bhatia has expressed ­interest in ­making a strategic ­minority ­investment in Liverpool Football Club,” the statement said.

It is believed that talks over the deal have been going on for three months.

FSG paid £300m to take ­control of Liverpool in 2010 and is poised to secure a spectacular return on its investment. The ­Boston‑based group, led by John W Henry, which also owns the ­Boston Red Sox and Pittsburgh ­Penguins, has pre­viously held discussions over a minority sale without reaching agreement but, with the Mittal family ­possessing an estimated net worth of £23bn, there is no doubt the buyers have the resources to execute the transaction.

Industry sources expressed surprise at the purported £4.5bn valuation but it is in line with recent deals.

Chelsea were bought four years ago by the Todd Boehly/Clearlake Capital group for an overall £4.25bn, although £2.5bn was to purchase the shares from Roman Abramovich. These proceeds were deposited into a frozen UK bank account while £1.75bn was a legally binding commitment for future investment directly into the club. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s purchase of 25% of Manchester United in 2024 valued the club at £4.3bn.

In an indication of the ­seriousness of the consortium’s bid for ­Liverpool, Bhatia resigned as a director of QPR on Tuesday after 19 years. The ­London-born entrepreneur has held numerous leadership roles at QPR since investing in the club in 2007. He said: “QPR has been a deeply important part of my life, and of my family’s life … I step back from my formal responsibilities with pride, gratitude and affection.”

Liverpool are in the US under their new head coach, Andoni Iraola, for a pre-season tour which begins with a game against Sunderland in ­Nashville on Saturday.

Sports.title: Manchester United supporters groups in uproar over suspension of season tickets
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s official Fans’ Forum, Manchester United Suppor­ters Trust (Must), The 1958 and five other such groups have complained to the club over supporters being “treated as suspects” after some had season tickets suspended as part of a move to stop the illegal reselling of seats.

United last week contacted fans who used six or more devices to access accounts linked to the club or to forward tickets, as in their view this suggested the potential buying of seats to resell. Members are allowed only to forward tickets to other members, or sell them back to United.

Those contacted were asked why multiple accounts were accessed, to identify the differing devices they used, and for photo ID to prove their validity. “Following a detailed review of acti­vity across our ­ticketing and digital platforms, we have ­identified sustained activity associated with your account, or with accounts that appear to be connected to or ­controlled by you, which may indicate a breach of the club’s ticketing terms and conditions,” the email from United said.

In a joint ­statement, ­supporter groups said: “Professional touting, automated purchasing and those who exploit ­supporters for ­financial gain have no place at ­Manchester United and deserve robust action. However, that action must be fair, ­proportionate and ­transparent. Longstanding supporters who have followed Manchester United for decades, often across multiple generations of the same family, should never feel they are being treated as suspects ­without clear evidence, due process or a meaningful opportunity to respond to the allegations made against them. The current approach has created a growing perception among supporters of ‘ban first and ask questions later’.

“The Fans’ Forum has rightly called on the club to pause the ­issuing of further suspensions and to halt any cancellation of season tickets while meaningful discussions take place. We support this.”

Reasons given by fans for the use of multiple devices to access club accounts includes being able to act for a group of friends or for elderly family members who struggle to use technology. United’s position is understood to be that no bans or formal sanctions have been applied and that any season tickets that have been revoked will be reissued before the team’s first home game of the season, which is against Ipswich Town on 30 August.

United have applied restrictions to accounts and offered only three days to appeal once a verdict is reached, as the club believe some of these are being used for illegal resale and the usual 14 days could be used to sell tickets on.

Sports.title: ‘The scrutiny is constant’: referee Anthony Taylor retires from football
Sports.content:
Anthony Taylor has announced his retirement from elite refereeing after a distinguished career spanning more than two decades and 831 matches.

One of England’s most accomplished officials, the 47-year-old officiated 668 matches in the professional game in England. He brings the curtain down on his career following his final appointment – the World Cup last‑16 game between Portugal and Spain in the US.

Reflecting on his career, Taylor said: “Officiating at the elite level has been an immense privilege, but the pressure is intense and the scrutiny is constant. The time is now right to step aside and look forward to transitioning to the next chapter of my career.

“I want to express my deepest gratitude to my two assistants, Gary and Adam, my refereeing colleagues and everyone connected with the game for all their support over the years. Most importantly, I want to thank my family and friends for their unwavering support throughout the immense sacrifices this career has demanded.”

Over 16 Premier League seasons, Taylor took charge of 432 top-flight matches and officiated every major domestic cup final. His honours include the FA Cup finals in 2017 and 2020, the 2015 League Cup final, the 2015 Community Shield and the 2018 Championship playoff final.

Taylor also enjoyed an outstanding international career, spending 14 years on the Fifa international list. During that time, he officiated at two World Cups (2022 and 2026), two European Championships (2020 and 2024) and two Club World Cups (2022 and 2025).

Quick Guide How do I 

Across the 163 international matches of which he took charge Taylor was entrusted with some of world football’s biggest fixtures, including the 2020 Uefa Super Cup, the 2021 Nations League final, the 2022 Club World Cup final, the 2023 Europa League final and the 2024 Champions League semi-final.

Howard Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, said: “Anthony has been a fantastic servant to the game over many years, both domestically and on the international stage. He has been repeatedly trusted to officiate in the biggest games including Portugal against Spain in this summer’s World Cup which ultimately capped off an outstanding career.

“He’s consistently demonstrated over a sustained period why he is one of the best and most successful officials that English football has ever produced, but it’s not just his on-field achievements that see him as a role model to many. The professionalism he’s shown and the support for his colleagues and the next generation of officials looking to follow in his footsteps is testament to his character.

“We thank him for his immense contribution to the game and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career.”

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos 'holds talks about investing in Liverpool' as Amazon founder - and world's fourth richest man worth $257BILLION - considers joining bid for Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Premier League giants Liverpool.

British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia is leading a group of financiers which is in talks to make a 'strategic minority investment' in Liverpool.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport on Tuesday, Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, is pushing for a deal with owners Fenway Sports Group that could take the club's value above £4.5billion ($6bn).

Now, though, Sky News reports that Bezos has been approached to join the consortium and has held discussions about working with Bhatia and Co. FSG and Bezos have been approached for comment.

FSG took control of Liverpool in 2010 for £300million and have since proven effective owners, giving the club the support they need to win two Premier League titles and a sixth Champions League.

Liverpool are largely self-sufficient, meaning FSG have not had to invest that much - figures published by the Athletic in 2024 indicated that they had only pumped in |£136m.

It remains uncertain whether Bezos, 62, will help fund a stake in the Premier League team. Bezos is ranked by Forbes as the fourth richest man in the world. He has a net worth of $256.9bn (£194.9bn).

Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Premier League giants Liverpool

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a small stake in Liverpool

Join the discussion Should mega-rich investors like Bezos be allowed to buy into iconic football clubs like Liverpool?

As reported by Sky News, the Amazon founder has previously considered bidding for the Seattle Seahawks - the reigning Super Bowl champions - and their NFL rivals, the Washington Commanders.

However, on neither occasion did Bezos proceed with a deal.

Bhatia, meanwhile, was co-owner at Championship side Queens Park Rangers. He has a stand named after him at the club's stadium, Loftus Road, but surprisingly stepped down from the QPR ownership setup on Tuesday.

A spokesperson for Fenway Sports Group said in a statement: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

Nothing is official yet and, if it was to proceed, it would follow a similar structure to a deal made three years ago when FSG sold a small stake to sports investment firm Dynasty.

Bezos founded Amazon in 1994, originally operating it out of his garage. It now has a revenue of $716bn (£534.83bn) - the most of any company in the world - and employs almost 1.6 million people.

FSG have 33 partners including principal owner John W Henry, chairman Tom Werner, president Michael Gordon, as well as NBA icon LeBron James.

They have typically ceded a reasonable amount of influence to managers, being nowhere near as interfering in day-to-day affairs like the owners of Chelsea, Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital.

Fans have often been frustrated that the club have not taken off the handbrake in the transfer window. The usual policy is for the club to be financially sustainable.

Andoni Iraola manages the Premier League giants, who are currently on tour in the USA

The world's richest people *According to Forbes 1) Elon Musk $794.5B net worth 2) Larry Page - $284.5B net worth 3) Sergey Brin - $262.4B net worth 4) Jeff Bezos - $256.9B net worth 5) Michael Dell - $228.4B net worth

Last summer, they sanctioned the biggest transfer window spend by a Premier League club ever, £446m, though their club revenues had freed up space for that under Profit & Sustainability Rules.

Liverpool are currently in Chicago as they begin their pre-season tour of the USA.

Andoni Iraola's side play Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday, followed by Wrexham in New York and Leeds back in Chicago, before returning home at the start of August.

Reds fans are excited to see defender Jeremy Jacquet, who signed from Rennes for £60m in January, but more incomings are anticipated.

It has been a slow summer at Anfield - the only other arrival is £34.5m World Cup winner Victor Munoz from Osasuna.

Iraola has identified two areas of concern and has issued an indirect appeal to transfer chiefs to kick on with summer plans.

'It is difficult to say a number when the market is open,' said the Basque. 'You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

'There are obvious situations where we know we need to sign players. Winger, for example. We definitely need to sign a winger. In other situations, we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what the cost is, how we see the players we have.

'We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust that are not in the ideal situation. It depends on a lot of things.'

Iraola also said Liverpool are 'very thin' in terms of defensive depth, with Conor Bradley out for several months more yet after a long-term knee injury.

Asked about potential exits, Iraola insisted Alisson will remain No 1 after intense interest from Juventus earlier in the window and added on World Cup runner-up Mac Allister: 'Alexis has been one of the best players of the club in the last years.

'He has had a very good World Cup so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. It always happens in the market. I want to keep my good players. I am looking more to sign new players than losing the ones we have.'

Sports.title: Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson reveals the 'emotional toll' of incorrect cancer diagnosis - three years on from receiving the all-clear after stage 3 cervical cancer battle
Sports.content:
Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson has opened up on receiving a second, incorrect, cancer diagnosis three years after she was given the all-clear following a year-long battle with stage 3 cervical cancer.

The broadcaster, 41, had been vocal about her journey with the disease, which saw her diagnosed after receiving a routine smear test in June 2022, and later undergo life-saving radiotherapy and chemotherapy treatment.

Wilson later produced a documentary on footballing figures who had similarly suffered with cancer, Football, Cancer and Me, which was released in November 2025.

But in a touching Instagram post, Wilson revealed that this year she had struggled after initially being told that cancer had returned.

'A little life update, please read until the end (red heart emoji),' she began.

Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson has revealed that she was incorrectly diagnosed with cancer a second time

While the broadcaster revealed that her relief is 'indescribable', she spoke up about the 'emotional toll' of the misdiagnosis on Instagram

'In February, after my three-year scan, I was told my cancer had returned in a lymph node. I couldn’t believe it - it felt like my whole world had crumbled all over again.

'But after being referred to the high-dose radiotherapy team, one consultant questioned whether the diagnosis was actually correct. What followed were five months of tests, scans, waiting and uncertainty before, last week, I finally got the news I’d been desperately hoping for: it wasn’t cancer after all. The lymph node is now thought to be a benign neuroma - a cluster of nerves that was likely inflamed at the time of my original scan.

'The relief was indescribable, but so too is the emotional toll from the last five months, believing - then not knowing if my cancer had returned. Living with that uncertainty was incredibly hard. On the outside, life carried on - I worked, was being a mum, played (lots of) padel, spent time with friends and family, and smiled for photos. But underneath it all, I was carrying something very heavy, and there were times I found myself in some very dark places.

'So why am I sharing this?

'Firstly, because we often talk about being “cancer free”, but I’m not sure any of us ever truly feel free of it. The fear of recurrence can stay with you long after treatment ends, and I think it’s important we talk about that reality. If you’re someone living beyond a cancer diagnosis, please know you’re not alone.

'Secondly, because social media is never the full picture. The last few months on here have probably looked like lots of happy moments, lovely places and time with people I love - and those moments were all real. But they existed alongside this. Instagram is a highlight reel, not the whole story.

'And finally, because we never really know what someone else is carrying. A friend, a colleague, the person serving you coffee or standing next to you in the supermarket - they could be fighting a battle you know nothing about.

'So this is simply a reminder to be kind. Always (red heart emoji). Thank you to my incredible support network, you know who you are.'

In response to the post, Wilson received warm words of support from colleagues including Emma Paton, Hayley McQueen, Izzy Christiansen and Emma Saunders, who herself was diagnosed with thyroid cancer before suffering serious brain infection encephalitis last year.

Wilson revealed in her documentary that her life had changed 'in an instant' with her 2022 diagnosis, which came shortly after the birth of her daughter Mabel.

'It hit me like a truck,' she said. 'I did wonder if I'm going to die. I'd prepared myself for the worst, I think you have to.

'I actually didn't tell anyone. I didn't want to put it on anyone. If one person can see this and make a phone call to the doctor because something doesn't feel right, then it's worth talking about.'

Wilson shared pictures while undergoing the tests necessary to confirm she is cancer-free

A permanent fixture at Sky Sports News, Wilson also produced a documentary, Football, Cancer and Me

The intensity of the treatment which followed included five weeks of daily radiotherapy, weekly chemotherapy and three days of invasive internal brachytherapy.

She explained how the hardest moments came when treatment forced her to be separated from her daughter for the first time, describing those three days in hospital as the darkest period of her illness.

Wilson, who lives in the Cotswolds with her partner of nine years Dan, later celebrated being told there was 'no evidence of disease' in March 2023 with a bottle of champagne and a jubilant post on social media.

Wilson, who hails from Perth in Scotland, graduated from Glasgow Caledonian University with a Masters in journalism in 2011, beginning as a graduate trainee at Sky Sports News that same year.

She later became a sub-editor and then a co-producer before making her screen debut on the channel in 2015.

Sports.title: NBA star Tyrese Haliburton marries his college sweetheart Jade Jones... weeks after devastating tragedy on her bachelorette party in St. Barts
Sports.content:
NBA star Tyrese Haliburton marries his college sweetheart Jade Jones... weeks after devastating tragedy on her bachelorette party in St. Barts

NBA superstar Tyrese Haliburton and his college sweetheart Jade Jones tied the knot on Tuesday - just weeks after their wedding celebrations were marred by the tragic death of a close friend.

The Indiana Pacers guard married Jones at the Indianapolis Marriage License Office. The couple were joined by a small group of loved ones ahead of their ceremony on August 1.

'It’s (courthouse) official,' Jones wrote on Instagram alongside a selection of photographs from outside the license office.

Haliburton was decked out in a dark t-shirt and pants, while his new wife wore a white dress and carried a bouquet of flowers.

Last month, Jones' friend mysteriously died during her bachelorette party in St. Barts at the age of 26. The former Iowa State cheerleader penned an emotional tribute to Makenzi Kern following her death.

'I am forever grateful that I got to love someone as truly special as Kenzi, and to have been loved back by her,' Jones wrote.

NBA star Tyrese Haliburton and his college sweetheart Jade Jones tied the knot on Tuesday

'It’s (courthouse) official,' Jones wrote on Instagram alongside a selection of photographs

The Indiana Pacers guard married Jones at the Indianapolis Marriage License Office

'Kenz was truly a light in this world, and that light will continue to shine in everyone who was lucky enough to know her. I love you forever until the end of time Kenzi.

'You are truly so beautiful inside and out & a once-in-a-lifetime kind of friend. Thank you for always showing up for me, for making me laugh until I cry, and for being such an unforgettable part of my life.

'I’ll always miss you but I know you’ll be with me, wherever I go. “See ya”'

Kern was pronounced dead on June 8, just two days after her birthday, while 'surrounded by her closest friends on a once in a lifetime trip to St. Barthelemy Island,' an online obituary says.

At the time, TMZ reported that Kern passed away unexpectedly from health complications, and her family does not suspect foul play, nor do they believe her death is related to drugs or alcohol.

She is survived by her parents, step parents, sister, step siblings, grandparents and her boyfriend.

Makenzi Kern (right) died while on a bachelorette party trip with her friend Jones (left)

Kern is seen here on the far right alongside the rest of the group, with Jones in the center

Kern attended Iowa State, where she was a cheerleading teammate of Jones'. That is where Jones met Haliburton, who played for the Cyclones before joining the NBA.

The couple began dating in 2019, while still at school. Haliburton proposed back on campus in 2025.

After leaving Iowa State, he was drafted by the Sacramento Kings in 2020 and was later traded to the Indian Pacers, whom he led to the 2025 NBA Finals.

Unfortunately, he suffered an Achilles injury during the Finals loss to Oklahoma City and consequently missed the 2025-26 season.

Sports.title: Madeleine McCann's younger brother, 21, to swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games as chemical engineering student sets his sights on Team GB spot for 2028 Olympics in LA
Sports.content:
Madeleine McCann's younger brother, 21, to swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games as chemical engineering student sets his sights on Team GB spot for 2028 Olympics in LA

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Madeleine McCann's younger brother will represent Scotland in swimming at the upcoming Commonwealth Games.

Sean McCann, 21, has been selected to compete for the Scots in the pool at the home Games, with swimming beginning Friday in Glasgow.

Madeleine disappeared from her family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, Portugal, at the age of three, back in 2007, and has been missing ever since. Sean was just two years old at the time.

19 years on, Sean is now making his senior international bow as a swimmer, and will compete alongside Olympic champion Duncan Scott for his national team.

McCann is a distance freestyler and is expected to compete in the 400m, 800m, and 1500m freestyle at the slimmed-down Games.

It is yet to be known whether parents Kate and Gerry McCann will attend the event to watch their son compete.

Madeline McCann's younger brother Sean will swim for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games

Sean will be swimming the 400m, 800m, and 1500m freestyle at the home Games in Glasgow

Sean has been competing in the pool since the age of eight, and his career took him to the international stage at youth level in 2023 as he competed at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad and Tobago.

The distance swimmer, who originally hails from Leicester but qualifies to represent Scotland through his father Gerry, is a student at Loughborough University, studying Chemical Engineering.

Loughborough is known for nurturing Great Britain's hottest prospects in the pool, with multiple Olympic champion Adam Peaty coming through the ranks at the performance centre.

Sean is looking to follow in the footsteps of the likes of Peaty by qualifying for the next Olympic Games in 2028.

There is confidence that his upcoming appearance has him on teh right path to competing for Team GB in LA in two years.

'I started competitive sport when I was 8, joining Charnwood Triathlon Club,' He once wrote on the Joe Humphries Memorial Trust website.

'It was here that I discovered my passion for swimming, and I joined Loughborough Town Swimming Club to increase the number of swim sessions I did per week.

'At the age of 10 I was selected to swim at City of Leicester (Leicestershire's performance swimming club), and I have since go on to win multiple county titles as well as becoming regional and National champion in my age group.

Madeline McCann went missing in 2007 when Sean was just two years old

'In order to have achieved this, I have had to remain extremely dedicated, getting up at 4am multiple mornings each week to train, since the age of 11.

'I am currently studying chemical engineering at Loughborough university, and train nine times a week in the pool, as well as three gym sessions, totalling over 20 hours of training week.

'I am aiming to compete at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and also the 2028 Olympics in LA.'

Sports.title: Dark truth of $1.5BILLION 'gas station heroin' secretly rife in sports after cops found it on tragic NBA star, 29, weeks before death
Sports.content:
On April 1, NBA star Brandon Clarke was arrested for overtaking multiple vehicles at more than 100mph in a no-passing zone in eastern Arkansas.

But the officers searching his Corvette had their attention attracted elsewhere. They found a blue duffle bag with multiple small packages containing green powder.

'It's just kratom, it is legal,' Clarke insisted. Kratom is legal in most states but was banned in Arkansas, where he had encountered police.

Six weeks later, Clarke was dead.

'Kratom is an addictive substance. It can, and does, kill,' Dr Josef G Thundiyil, a medical toxicologist and emergency physician with Orlando Health, told the Daily Mail.

Kratom is sold legally in smoke shops, convenience stores and online. Marketed as a natural wellness product, kratom, which has since been dubbed 'gas station heroin,' has grown into an estimated $1.5billion-a-year industry, according to the American Kratom Association.

Memphis Grizzlies star Brandon Clarke died at the age of 29 in May of this year

Police in Arkansas found kratom, otherwise known as 'gas station heroin,' on Clarke during his arrest weeks before his death

In the same botanical family as coffee, kratom is derived from the leaves of a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia and has been used there for centuries. Only recently has it gained in popularity in the US for purported pain relief and stamina benefits.

Sold in brightly-colored cans resembling energy drinks, capsules pass as everyday vitamins or sugar-coated gummies. But experts say looks are deceiving.

'That it's sold very unregulated in tea shops, smoke shops, gives a false reassurance,' Dr Thundiyil explained.

He warned, a 'whole host' of negative and dangerous side effects have been reported amid kratom's boom, including 'severe compulsive addiction.'

'Users describe: I feel it's just as bad as when I was on an opioid, meaning it's very addictive,' he continued. 'And what we have found of the different outcomes, we've seen reported things like seizures and liver failure. But the one that really caught our attention was death.'

A government report showed poison center calls about kratom have skyrocketed. In 2025 alone, they jumped 1,200 percent to 3,400. There were 233 kratom-associated deaths reported between 2015 and 2025, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Many incidents are a consequence of kratom being mixed with alcohol or other drugs.

'[Kratom] has two different ways of working,' Dr Zaid Fadul, a board-certified physician and founder of Bespoke Concierge MD, told Daily Mail. 'At low doses, it can be a stimulant and can cause pain relief.

In the same botanical family as coffee, kratom comes from leaves of a tree native to Asia

Kratom comes in brightly-colored cans resembling energy drinks and capsules look like candy

'Higher doses have different effects. It can be sedating. Any dose for a prolonged period of time, you get chemical dependence, then eventually addiction.'

The risks don't end there. Dehydration is a side effect, triggered by the loss of appetite caused by kratom, Dr Fadul said.

'Two, kratom is going to mask pain,' he added. 'It's not going to treat pain.'

Kratom does not treat injuries. Instead, it lessens pain for athletes to continue training and competing.

'That's when a stress fracture turns into a real fracture,' Dr Fadul said. 'You want recovery for athletes. You don't want pain masking. You want real recovery.'

In an industry where the body is the money-maker, preserving health is key - and kratom puts that in jeopardy.

Given its accessibility and legal status, it is a product athletes may not necessarily have to disclose to teams and risk a trade.

'I get that athletes are hesitant to take opioids, or they want to get off opioids, and so they're looking for alternatives,' Dr Thundiyil said. 'My warning would be kratom is probably not that solution; it's unproven.

Clarke died near Los Angeles, where he had been staying with a friend from college

An investigation into the power forward's death is still ongoing

'The harms are growing. You may be jumping out the pot and into the fire.'

Clarke was discovered with 235 grams of kratom in April.

The Canadian-American star was restricted to two games for the Grizzlies' last season with injury. He missed 73 games, sitting out 26 recovering from surgery on his right knee before another 46 with a right calf strain.

In addition to kratom, Clarke had a THC vape pen and a prescription for a common painkiller used to treat sporting injuries when he was arrested

'That right there is legal pain medicine,' Clarke said in the dashcam video of his arrest. 'That's Toradol.'

Six weeks later, Clarke was found dead on May 12 in the San Fernando Valley. His death is being investigated as a potential overdose after drug paraphernalia was found at the scene.

No official cause has been announced and the inquest is ongoing.

Clarke and a woman attend his sister's 2024 wedding in Mexico City, Mexico

Clarke poses for a picture with his mother, Whitney Triplett, his step father and his half siblings

Clarke is not alone.

UFC veteran Diego Sanchez's former coach Joshua Fabia accused him of being 'strung out' on kratom and other substances in 2021. Fabia claimed the fighter was an 'addict' following their split. Sanchez denied the allegations.

Wrestler Sabu was allegedly given kratom ahead of his final match amid fears he would not show up to the ring, fellow wrestler Joey Janela claimed in a 2025 interview. Janela later claimed that Sabu - whose real name was Terrance Brunk - took kratom 'daily for years' to help him get off other substances.

Sabu died at age 61 in May 2025 three weeks after his final match. GCW, which hosted the bout, denied any involvement in his death.

Meanwhile, the United Football League - the eight-team spring football league - embraced CBD Kratom in 2024 as its official partner, highlighting potential to 'enhance physical performance’ as well as ‘kratom's ability to aid in chronic pain’.

The Missouri Attorney General's Office launched an investigation into CBD Kratom in November for 'deception, fraud, false promises' among other acts. It is one of nearly two dozen kratom companies under investigation by the Missouri AG office. The UFL's partnership ended before the start of this season.

CBD Kratom, meanwhile, said it relished an 'opportunity to demonstrate the strength of our safety standards, compliance practices, and long-standing commitment to consumer education.'

UFC veteran Diego Sanchez (right) denied accusations of being 'strung out' on kratom

Kratom is not considered performance-enhancing by the World Anti-Doping Agency. It was briefly monitored by WADA but removed from the tracking list in 2018.

The United States Anti-Doping Agency, which handles the drug testing for Olympians, explicitly advises against using it over health hazards, but has not banned it.

In Tennessee, where Clarke played for the Grizzlies, kratom was legal when he was arrested. Three months later, Tennessee became the latest state to ban it, with the illegal status enforced from July 1.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's full humiliation laid bare: Left crying as his Argentine thugs disgraced themselves... how this World Cup exposed the GOAT's dark arts shame
Sports.content:
Like so many sporting greats, Lionel Messi did not get the fairytale ending that his illustrious career deserved in New Jersey on Sunday night.

Throughout history it has proven a rarity for legendary athletes to exit the big stage on a high. Muhammad Ali lost three of his final four fights before hanging up his gloves. Michael Jordan bowed out from the NBA after failing to make the playoffs for a second straight year with the Washington Wizards. Tom Brady waved goodbye to football after a postseason loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Babe Ruth, Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal... the list runs long. And now Messi's name has been added to it. Well, at least when it comes to the World Cup.

The sad sight of Argentina's icon shedding tears after their final defeat to Spain says it all. At 39, it is almost certain this was his closing chapter on soccer's grandest stage. He will be 43 when the next one rolls around.

Yet Messi didn't just sign off from the World Cup on the back of a loss. It was as miserable and shameful of a night as it could be for his country at MetLife Stadium.

After becoming the first finalists in history to fail to register a single shot in 90 minutes - and not testing Spain's goalkeeper Unai Simon once in 120 - Argentina's sore losers resorted to thuggery when Spain celebrated their triumph at full-time.

Lionel Messi did not get his fairytale ending as Argentina lost to Spain in the World Cup final

The Argentina icon exited the biggest stage in soccer on the most depressing of notes

Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the biggest villain, grabbing Spain's Eric Garcia by the neck and punching midfielder Gavi in the face before pushing him over. Defender Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso, while even a 53-year-old Argentine assistant coach landed a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo.

While he was not involved in the violence, Messi is captain of this team and what will likely prove his World Cup finale will always be remembered for the ugly scenes at full time.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner didn't cover himself in glory, either. In the wake of a red card for Argentina's Enzo Fernandez, Messi embarrassed himself with an attempt to send Marc Cucurella down the tunnel.

After Cucurella spoke to him while briefly covering his mouth, Messi stuck his arm in the air and signaled to the referee to try and get the Spain man sent off. FIFA's new rules forbid players from concealing conversations.

Fortunately, the official did not bow to the pressure of one of the game's finest ever players. But the sight of an all-time great, renowned for modesty on and off the field, resorting to dirty tactics was grim.

'One of the most pathetic things I've ever seen from a supposed sportsman,' Piers Morgan fumed on X about the incident. 'Messi's fake halo shattered in this World Cup; he was the sneaky cheating leader of a vile bunch of violent thugs.'

Once they'd grown tired of lashing out, the now-former world champions made it a masterclass in bitterness by refusing to form a guard of honor for Spain and turning their backs as their competitors lifted the World Cup.

They then sparked ugly scenes at full time by lashing out at Spain as they celebrated the win

Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the neck and punching Gavi before pushing him over

Messi also embarrassed himself with his desperate attempt to get Marc Cucurella sent off

Cucurella briefly touched his mouth while talking to Messi - players are sent off for covering their face while talking to opponents

The closing shot of Messi at a World Cup will forever be crying with his back to the trophy lift, surrounded by his henchmen, in a moment more befitting of 10-year-old children than elite athletes.

If that wasn't bad enough, Argentina skipped mandatory post-game media interviews and fled the stadium.

Messi is known for humility while cementing his status as arguably the greatest of all time, with the petulant antics of famous rival Cristiano Ronaldo - often accused of hogging the limelight and not being a good teammate - painting him in a better light.

Nevertheless, soccer's golden boy bid farewell to the World Cup with most wanting him to lose. He did exactly that, without managing a shot on target before Argentina disgraced themselves.

Other than fan footage of her leaving the stadium under the protection of burly security guards, there were also mysteriously few sightings of Messi's stunning wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at Sunday's final.

It was a far cry from her usually-frequent appearances at the front of the stadium's VIP suites, cheering her man on alongside their children. How poignant, then, for her to be in hiding as Messi struggled and wept on a devastating day.

There were few sightings of Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at the final other than her leaving

It took Antonela a day before she paid tribute to her husband on social media after the loss

She broke her silence a day later, writing on Instagram: 'You will always be the best. Thank you for showing us every day that true success is built through hard work, sacrifice, and perseverance - without ever losing sight of who you really are.

'You are the best example for our children and an inspiration to millions of people. I admire you more than words can express, and I feel immensely proud to walk through life by your side.'

All in all, it was an anticlimactic end for the Messi family at his sport's most prestigious competition.

Even his all-time World Cup goals record no longer remains. Less than a month after leapfrogging Germany icon Miroslav Klose in Argentina's second group-stage outing against Austria, France superstar Kylian Mbappe's brace in the third-place playoff took him one ahead of Messi on 21.

So what next? Messi has half the season to finish with Inter Miami, who return to action Wednesday after MLS's World Cup break.

But Messi won't play in their first game back against Chicago Fire, nor their trip to CF Montreal on Saturday.

According to ESPN, he'll also skip the MLS All-Star Game on July 29, too. It would be the third time Messi has been selected for the annual showpiece. He is yet to play in a single one.

A more likely return is Miami's clash with Columbus Crew on Saturday August 1.

Once back up and running at club level, Messi has over two years remaining on his current deal with the team, which extends beyond the 2028 Copa America.

Messi may stick around at club level for a while but he will surely retire from Argentina duty

When he's still operating at such a high level - he still scored eight World Cup goals this year - it would be a shock to see him end that contract early.

As for his international career, it remains to be seen whether Messi calls it a day after two consecutive World Cup final appearances. It would make most sense.

Prior to the final he hinted as such by referring to it as 'The Last Tango' in a post on social media. Following the defeat, he also shared an emotional message on Instagram which felt like a farewell.

'The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal,' he wrote. 'But I also hold onto all the good things.

'Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.'

Presumably through gritted teeth, he added: 'I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship.'

If only he and Argentina could have done a better job of that on the field.

Sports.title: New boss Vrancken laments Hearts' failings after nightmare first match in charge
Sports.content:
Wouter Vrancken bemoaned his players’ lack of efficiency in both boxes as Hearts slumped to a nightmare 4-0 defeat in the first leg of their Champions League second qualifying round tie in Austria.

It was a horrendous first match in charge for Belgian coach Vrancken who replaced Derek McInnes in the Hearts hot seat this summer.

Despite dominating possession and having more touches in the opposition box than Sturm Graz, Vrancken’s side suffered a crushing loss which effectively ends their hopes of further progress in Europe’s elite club competition.

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken despairs as his new charges suffer in Austria

Hearts were guilty of shocking defending, especially at set pieces, as goals from Jon Stankovic, Jeyland Mitchell, Luca Weindhandl and Jurgen Heil put Graz in total control.

The visitors also missed several clear-cut chances of their own with Pierre Landry-Kabore and Alexander Kyziridis especially culpable when the score was still 1-0.

‘We didn’t start too badly but then conceded from a set piece,’ said Vrancken. ‘That was the summary of the game, we got killed by two set pieces at the start of the first half and second half.

‘After the first goal, we needed some minutes to come back into it and find our confidence again. We did pretty well and created a lot of chances which we needed to do much better with.

‘They were 100 per cent chances and at this level, you have to score them. I was pretty confident at half-time that we could still turn it around.

‘Then the second half started and after we missed the first good opportunity again, we conceded from another set piece.

Graz celebrate after Stankovic scores the early opening goal for Graz

‘Then it is difficult in their heads for the players. Sometimes you try to force it and make it more difficult for yourself. When you don’t kill (teams) yourself, you get killed. It’s a pity.

‘We had to be more efficient and Sturm Graz were more efficient than us tonight. It’s no excuse. We showed in the game that we had a lot of possession and created a lot of chances from it.’

Hearts now look set to drop into the Europa League, where they would face either Benfica or St Gallen in the third qualifying round, but Vrancken insists he hasn’t given up hope of overseeing a dramatic comeback in the return leg against Sturm Graz at Tynecastle next Tuesday.

‘You have to believe it,’ he said. ‘Especially at Tynecastle with the support of our fans. The ones who were here tonight were amazing, even with this result.

‘So we have go full out next week. If we are more efficient in the first half, then you never know. We could score some goals and there could be magic there. In this scenario, we still have to believe it.'

Sports.title: Sturm Graz 4-0 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's bold vision falls apart on a night of disorganised disaster with Jam Tarts' Champions League hopes in tatters
Sports.content:
Sturm Graz 4-0 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's bold vision falls apart on a night of disorganised disaster with Jam Tarts' Champions League hopes in tatters

Wouter Vrancken describes the style of play he likes to instil in his teams as ‘organised chaos’.

On a truly calamitous night in southern Austria, it was quite simply a disorganised disaster as the Belgian coach saw his Hearts tenure get off to the worst possible start.

It was all risk and no reward for the Gorgie club as Sturm Graz took an iron grip on this Champions League second qualifying round tie.

Defensively, Hearts were an absolute mess as Graz captain Jon Stankovic’s fourth minute opener was followed by a flurry of three goals in a torrid nine-minute spell early in the second half.

Barring a remarkable turnaround at Tynecastle next Tuesday night, Hearts will be dropping down into the Europa League qualifiers where it won’t get much easier for Vrancken.

The 47-year-old clearly needs time to bed his ideas in but will quickly find himself under serious pressure unless he restores some of the defensive discipline which was the hallmark of Hearts’ effectiveness under Derek McInnes last season.

Vrancken is left with questions to answer following a 4-0 hammering in Austria

It had been just 68 days since they lost out on the Premiership title in such agonising circumstances at Celtic Park and amid the pain experienced by club and supporters that afternoon, it was easy to lose sight of the fact they had still secured Champions League participation for the first time in 20 years.

Despite all of the close season upheaval at Tynecastle, with the departures of manager McInnes and key playing duo Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin to Rangers, new boss Vrancken relied on as many established squad members as possible for his opening night in the job.

Only two of Hearts new signings - defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott and winger Calvin Miller - were in the starting line-up named by Vrancken.

If he was looking to establish some early stability, however, Vrancken instead suffered disruption with the cheap and early concession of Sturm Graz’s opener.

It was Hearts who seemed to have made the brighter start, Christian Borchgrevink firing a shot over after Graz keeper Daniil Khudiakov unconvincingly palmed out Harry Milne’s low cross in the opening minute.

That sign of encouragement for the travelling fans was wiped out as Hearts completely switched off at the back when Jeyland Mitchell launched a long throw into their penalty area from the left. Jamie McCart was caught on his heels as Stankovic rose to guide a simple close range header beyond Alexander Schwolow.

The expansive and pacy attacking style of play Vrancken is renowned for was certainly evident but while Hearts looked good in possession, they remained wide open at the back.

Stankovic celebrates after Sturm Graz go 1-0 up inside four minutes

Graz missed a glaring opportunity to double their lead in the 10th minute when Simon Seidl’s corner was flicked on by Stankovic before Seedy Jatta hit a post with a free header from inside the six yard box.

When Schwolow had to react smartly to keep out a deflected shot from Jacob Hodl, there was a danger of the tie running away from Hearts.

They carved out plenty of menacing opportunities of their own, however, against a Graz defence which also appeared vulnerable.

After Claudio Braga had a low shot held by Khudiakov, Hearts should have equalised in the 25th minute. Oisin McEntee’s surging run carved a path into the Graz penalty area and the Irish midfielder showed great awareness to pick out Pierre Landry Kabore with his cutback.

It was a bread and butter chance for the big striker but with only Khudiakov to beat, he steered his shot straight into the grateful arms of the Russian keeper.

Graz went straight up the other end and Fagan-Walcott spared the blushes of his central defensive partner McCart who had played Jatta onside. The Norwegian striker looked certain to score until Fagan-Walcott slid in to make a brilliant block.

New arrival Guendouz is left frustrated after failing to make an impact

Neither side were willing to resort to a cautious approach as the contest continued to ebb and flow. Hearts wasted their best chance yet to level matters in the 34th minute. Braga won the ball high up the pitch and slid it to Alexandros Kyziridis who was unmarked inside the box.

It was the definition of a sitter but the Greek winger inexplicably sidefooted his shot wide of Khudiakov’s left hand post.

There was an anxious moment for Hearts six minutes before half-time when Hungarian referee Gergo Bogar pointed to the spot after Milne had slid in to block a shot from Szymon Wlodarczyk. While the ball hit the full-back’s arm, it did so only after bouncing up off his leg and a VAR review correctly saw the decision overturned.

Hearts’ start to the second half was the stuff of nightmares as Graz ran riot. The visitors were undone by another simple set piece when Mitchell had a free back post run to head home half-time sub Otar Kiteishvili’s corner from the left in the 50th minute.

Three minutes later, it was 3-0 when teenager Luca Weinhandl’s deflected shot beat Schwolow after Hearts made a mess of several chances to clear the danger.

They were carved wide open again in the 59th minute as Jurgen Heil played a one-two with Weinhandl on the right of the box before slamming the ball home.

Vrancken made a raft of changes in the closing half hour but Tom Renaud’s shot over was the closest Hearts came to pulling a goal back and perhaps giving them a sliver of hope for the second leg.

As it is, their long-awaited return to the Champions League looks as good as over.

Sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau controversy at The Open costs LIV Golf star more than £200,000
Sports.content:
Bryson DeChambeau controversy at The Open costs LIV Golf star more than £200,000

LIV Golf star Bryson DeChambeau's two-stroke penalty at the Open Championship for a rules violation ended up costing him to the tune of more than £200,000

View 2 Images Bryson DeCheambeau's penalty at The Open came at a heavy cost (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

Bryson DeChambeau's unfortunate two-stroke penalty at The Open Championship left him £200,000 poorer when all was said and done. The two-time US Open champion was handed a two-stroke penalty during the second round at Royal Birkdale after flattening the grass during his backswing.

‌



Officials judged that the action handed the American a better lie and warranted punishment. He maintained he was simply reading his line by positioning himself directly behind the ball, not that it had any effect in easing his penalty.

‌



DeChambeau, 32, even threatened to walk away from the tournament in protest despite moving up to second at one stage. The trip to Merseyside also marked the first time he has managed to make the cut at a final in 2026.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

The American headed straight to the driving range after R&A officials docked his score on the leaderboard. DeChambeau ignored waiting journalists and had a hand in forcing third-round tee times to be pushed back as attention remained fixed on the dispute.

Bryson DeChambeau shows true colours with response to Rory McIlroy taunts at The Open READ MORE :

Bryson DeChambeau wanted Donald Trump's help after controversy at The Open READ MORE :

Several fellow players weighed in on the controversy, with Scottie Scheffler among them as he insisted his countryman is "not a cheater." Rory McIlroy had his own take on the matter and described the incident as "performative."

‌



DeChambeau subsequently said the penalty only fired him up further and spurred him on. However, he ultimately fell short of lifting the Claret Jug, finishing in a tie for 14th place and pocketing £175,000.

Had the two-stroke penalty not been applied, DeChambeau would have walked away with £384,000 and a share of sixth place alongside Casey Jarvis, Lucas Herbert and Si Woo Kim. DeChambeau has avoided the media since the incident occurred.

View 2 Images DeChambeau's two-stroke penalty at Royal Birkdale caused him to slide down the final standings (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Yet numerous current and former Tour professionals, including Scheffler, have argued this represents a more complex issue than a straightforward penalty. The Texan said: "I think maybe we need to be a little bit more strict in the way that we are policing guys.

"But it's a little bit of a balance because you've got certain guys like a Bryson who, every shot he hits is going to be shown on TV. When you have camera angles that are far away, things can look different than they do when you're right there.

I've never seen him cheat once, whether we were having a putting contest on the putting green or chipping contest, or anytime we played amateur golf, I never saw anything suspicious."

DeChambeau is now set to compete at LIV Golf UK this week. His Crushers GC team is seeking its third win of the year, while DeChambeau himself is chasing a third individual victory of 2026.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola now has something Arne Slot and Jurgen Klopp never did at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola now has something Arne Slot and Jurgen Klopp never did at Liverpool

Andoni Iraola has been in charge of Liverpool for a matter of weeks and has already enjoyed something not seen at Anfield since 2010

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola has plenty to work with in his first Liverpool season (Image: PETER POWELL, AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola is just a few weeks into his tenure but already has something never enjoyed by Arne Slot or Jurgen Klopp. Not only that but it's something only present in one Reds season in the Premier League era.

‌



Thanks to new signing Victor Munoz's presence in Spain's victorious World Cup squad, Iraola has two World Cup winners at his disposal at the same time. You have to go back more than a decade for the last time that was the case.

‌



Munoz might not have played for La Roja at the tournament as he struggled with injury but the former Osasuna winger still has a winner's medal. Liverpool's other World Cup winner is of course Alexis Mac Allister, though the midfielder was still on Brighton's books when he started for Argentina in the 2022 final.

‌



It's also the first time ever that Liverpool have had two World Cup winners from different countries at the same time. The last time they had two world champions was in 2010, as Pepe Reina and Fernando Torres both won with Spain.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Torres didn't stick around for long, though. He joined Chelsea midway through the following season, leaving Reina as the sole survivor.

There's only one other example of the Reds having multiple World Cup winners at the same time. Roger Hunt, Ian Callaghan and Gerry Byrne were all part of the England squad that claimed the trophy on home turf in 1966 and were all Liverpool players when they achieved the feat.

View 2 Images Victor Munoz arrives fresh off a World Cup triumph (Image: Marvin Ibo Guengoer - GES Sportfoto, Getty Images)

‌



Munoz completed his £34m move during the World Cup as Liverpool beat Newcastle to a player who turned 23 during the tournament. "With Victor, I think we signed him in a moment where he's very hungry, he's ambitious, but he's still humble and knows that he has to come very ready," new boss Iraola said.

"I think he's someone with some versatility – can play right, can play left, he has the work-rate also for all that we will require. Looking forward to having him here, even if we know that we will have to wait with him and Macca."

Iraola is taking a 31-man squad to the United States for pre-season but Munoz and Mac Allister will both be afforded additional time off following their World Cup exertions. Liverpool have matches against Sunderland, Wrexham and Leeds on the other side of the Atlantic before heading back home for a pair of friendlies at Anfield in August.

Sports.title: Arsenal could boost transfer war chest by £90m with four exits in the works
Sports.content:
Arsenal could boost transfer war chest by £90m with four exits in the works

Arsenal could boost their transfer budget

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta is ready for a host of new arrivals (Image: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

Arsenal could increase their summer budget by at least £90million if players such as Gabriel Jesus and Ben White are offloaded. The Gunners have secured Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier on permanent transfers with Christos Tzolis poised to become the third new arrival.

‌



Arsenal have invested £68.5m so far and Mikel Arteta will also seek to trim down his squad. Leandro Trossard has already left north London, moving to Besiktas for £15.3m.

‌



Jakub Kiwior has also departed, generating £14m following a successful loan spell at Porto that triggered a permanent transfer. The Gunners could strengthen their finances further with four additional transactions in the pipeline.

‌



Gabriel Jesus has been linked with a potential departure in recent weeks as the striker has just 12 months remaining on his deal. The Brazilian ranks among the highest-paid players in north London despite a recent shortage of playing time owing to injuries.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal to receive millions in FIFA compensation after disastrous World Cup blow READ MORE :

The Athletic reports that the club values Jesus between £18m and £20m with Serie A outfit AC Milan having expressed interest. Calciomercato suggested that both parties could finalise a deal for approximately £16m with separate reports indicating that the Italian side are in discussions.

‌



Fellow Brazilian Gabriel Martinelli is also attracting transfer interest from several clubs, with Calciomercato reporting that Manchester United, Newcastle and Bayern Munich are all keeping tabs on the winger. It is understood that the Gunners will sanction a sale for £42.6m as they await the arrival of new signing Tzolis to fill his boots.

Experienced defender Ben White is another Arsenal figure touted for a departure. The 28-year-old managed just 12 Premier League appearances last season, with Jurrien Timber emerging as the preferred option at right-back.

3 View 3 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus are linked with exits (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media/Getty Images) 3 View 3 Images Christian Norgaard and Ben White may also leave (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal are believed to be holding out for a minimum of £25m for White, with Everton said to be keen on securing his signature. However, injuries to both Timber and William Saliba could scupper those plans, with the right-back likely to be called upon in the near term.

Finally, Christian Norgaard could net Arsenal an additional £4.2m. The Mail reports that Crystal Palace are weighing up a move for the 32-year-old midfielder.

It is suggested that Norgaard's Premier League experience could bolster the Eagles' midfield. The defensive midfielder is valued at around £4.2m and could be available at a reasonable price given that his contract is set to expire next summer.

Sports.title: Man Utd may have to change plans for two players after Marcus Rashford return
Sports.content:
Man Utd may have to change plans for two players after Marcus Rashford return

Marcus Rashford is set to return to Manchester United's first-team squad after Barcelona failed to activate a £26m permanent transfer clause

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford could yet play a part for Manchester United next season (Image: Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford's return to the Manchester United first-team squad could have significant implications for both Patrick Dorgu and Matheus Cunha. It has been a deeply frustrating summer for the Reds Devils' homegrown talent.

‌



The winger's coveted switch to Barcelona appears increasingly unlikely to come to fruition after the Catalan club failed to trigger a £26million clause in last campaign's loan agreement to secure his permanent transfer. United are seeking alternative permanent suitors, with Bayern Munich and Tottenham Hotspur amongst the clubs reportedly in the frame.

‌



The club are keen to offload his £325,000-a-week wages in order to safeguard their newly implemented pay structure. Yet with no permanent deal for the winger on the horizon, United could find themselves having little choice but to cut their losses and send him out on loan once more before the window shuts.

‌



Alternatively, United may have to concede they cannot permanently remove his wages from the books and bring him back into the first-team fold. There will be optimism at Old Trafford in that scenario that Carrick could unlock the best from the England international, much as he did with numerous players during his interim tenure last season.

Alejandro Garnacho set to swap places with Morgan Rogers as Aston Villa eye swoop READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

However, his reintegration into United's squad as another left-wing option will undoubtedly affect several key figures in Carrick's setup.

‌



Dorgu is one such player. The Danish wing-back found himself without a natural role in United's setup after Ruben Amorim's 3-4-2-1 formation was abandoned under Carrick.

Yet the 21-year-old demonstrated real potential in Rashford's left-wing berth, delivering eye-catching displays in memorable victories against Manchester City and Arsenal. The question remains whether he would be content with a reduced role having enjoyed so much game time under Carrick last term.

Rashford's comeback could equally affect Cunha, who served as United's primary left-wing option. The Brazilian made a strong impression with 10 goals and four assists, playing a pivotal part in the Reds' third-placed finish and their return to Champions League football.

‌



View 2 Images Patrick Dorgu could be impacted by Marcus Rashford's return (Image: 2026 Manchester United FC)

Cunha was not recruited as a squad player, though his form last season looks certain to secure him a starting spot at the very least heading into 2026/27. One possible solution for Carrick would be to utilise the 27-year-old as a centre-forward — a role he filled on several occasions last term — with Benjamin Sesko still sidelined with a shin injury.

BBC Sport reports that Rashford, who has two years left to run on his contract, is "relaxed" about the prospect of returning to train with the United squad. The 28-year-old is also understood to have a far more positive relationship with former teammate Carrick, in stark contrast to his "confrontational relationship" with ex-United boss Amorim.

‌



Rashford contributed 14 goals and 14 assists for Barcelona last season, claiming the La Liga title in the process. Following the conclusion of his World Cup duties, Rashford posted on social media with an optimistic message.

He said: "Keep believing in us. Our time will come. Now it's time for me to rest, reflect, spend some quality time with family and friends, and come back a better version of myself."

Sports.title: Man Utd only have room for two more specific signings as Premier League rule forces hand
Sports.content:
Man Utd only have room for two more specific signings as Premier League rule forces hand

Manchester United have already completed three transfers this summer but their future plans will have to revolve around league restrictions

View 2 Images Manchester United are working on more arrivals as the season draws closer (Image: Manchester United, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been busy this summer, adding Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow to their ranks. However, Premier League squad rules look like complicating their future plans unless they can make some sales.

‌



Santos and Tielemans arrived for more than £80m between them while Darlow joined on a free transfer from Leeds. There have also been exits - Casemiro and Andre Onana notable among them - but there could still be complications when it comes to naming their 25-man Premier League squad for the new season.

‌



League rules mean that 25-player allowance needs to be made up of 17 non-homegrown players and eight who qualify as homegrown. The latter category doesn't need to be players trained by United specifically - English and Welsh-trained players will also count, including new goalkeeper Darlow.

‌



Players aged 21 or under (born on or after January 1, 2005) don't get counted against either allowance but age threshold means United players born in 2004 no longer qualify as part of the Under-21 exemption for the 2026/27 season. Patrick Dorgu now takes up a non-homegrown slot, while Dan Gore and Toby Collyer occupy homegrown berths.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd ahead of Arsenal in Manu Kone race after opening transfer talks for £51m star READ MORE :

Michael Carrick issues next Man Utd transfer demand as Premier League stars targeted READ MORE :

Gore featured against Wrexham in Saturday's pre-season friendly but could still be moved on despite an impressive performance, as might Collyer after ending last season out on loan. Goalkeeper Radek Vitek - also classified as homegrown - is anticipated to depart despite appearing at the weekend.

‌



Alongside Dorgu, the non-homegrown group currently stands at 15 and features new arrivals Santos and Tielemans. The group is rounded out by Senne Lammens, Altay Bayındır, Noussair Mazraoui, Matthijs de Ligt, Lisandro Martínez, Diogo Dalot, Manuel Ugarte, Bruno Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, Joshua Zirkzee and Benjamin Sesko.

To qualify as homegrown, a player does not need to be British as long as they have spent three seasons on an English or Welsh club's books by the end of the season in which they turn 21. This means winger Amad, who arrived at United as a teenager, is eligible to occupy one of the homegrown places.

View 2 Images Ivorian winger Amad qualifies as homegrown (Image: David Horton - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



Amad is among 11 homegrown players aged over 21, alongside the previously mentioned Gore, Collyer and Vitek as well as Tom Heaton, Karl Darlow, Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount, Marcus Rashford and Dermot Mee. That said, a number of those individuals may well have moved on from Old Trafford before the campaign kicks off.

Vitek, Gore and Collyer are possibly the most likely to exit, with Vitek already indicating a desire for regular first-team football. Should all three depart, it would still leave United with eight homegrown players while freeing up two additional slots for non-homegrown recruits.

The non-homegrown quota could still rise. Bayindir may join fellow goalkeeper Onana in the Turkish Super Lig, while United might yet choose to omit Ugarte from their 25-man squad if his serious injury sustained on World Cup duty means he wouldn't play anyway.

‌



So, while the number of available places might appear limited at present, there is every possibility it can expand. There is already room for Manu Kone amid speculation linking the France midfielder, while new signing Tynan Thompson won't count towards any quota as he is under the age of 21.

Matters could become complicated should another one of those homegrown players depart, however, with Rashford amongst those with an uncertain future. More exits could potentially prompt United to sign another homegrown player if they wish to fulfil their complete quota of 25 players in their official Premier League squad.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bargain World Cup hero eyed as path opens to £80m Andoni Iraola transfer reunion
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bargain World Cup hero eyed as path opens to £80m Andoni Iraola transfer reunion

Liverpool's transfer odds have taken a serious turn for the better as Andoni Iraola chases a World Cup icon, while the possibility of an emotional reunion has emerged

View 2 Images Ferran Torres is reportedly a target for Liverpool after his World Cup final heroics (Image: FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

Transfer season is picking up at Anfield despite the fact Andoni Iraola's Liverpool are no longer in the building. The squad has jetted to the United States for its pre-season tour, which has coincided with a sudden spike of activity on the rumours front.

‌



Now that World Cup 2026 is done and dusted, fans can expect business to pick up in a big way. And Iraola is all but certain to be more active in the coming weeks as he gets to grips with the talents at his disposal.

‌



One World Cup star in particular looks destined to be on the move, with news that the Reds have entered the race. The ECHO has taken a deeper dive into that and more as the latest transfer headlines spell good news at Anfield.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Reds compete for World Cup hero Torres

Ferran Torres is reportedly being lined up for a return to the Premier League if Liverpool get their way. The news comes on the back of Spain's extra-time triumph over Argentina in Sunday's World Cup final, where he scored the only goal.

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

Barcelona winger Torres came off the bench to power La Roja over the finish line in New Jersey and write his name in the history books. And that finish may help in clinching a move to Anfield this summer.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain have been most closely linked with the player, as well as Liverpool wing target Yan Diomande. Added to the fact Les Parisiens already have Bradley Barcola, the Reds' other primary target for that position, and a showdown looks inevitable at some point this summer.

However, Torres would come a lot cheaper than those other two names given he's older and is now in the final 12 months of his contract at the Camp Nou. L'Equipe has reported Liverpool are ready to challenge PSG for his cut-price signature, which is allegedly valued somewhere between £40million and £50m.

‌



That's less than half the kind of fees being associated with Diomande and Barcola. Meanwhile, Torres would arguably be a more natural fit given he's more accustomed to playing on the right flank, which is where the Reds have a Salah-shaped void.

It's been so long since Torres spent 18 months at Manchester City before departing for Barca in January 2022, yet he's still in his prime years after turning 26 in February. Why Barca aren't keen on extending the terms of a player who scored 21 goals in all competitions last season, only they will know, but the Catalans' loss could be Liverpool's gain.

In fact, Torres has averaged 20 goals per season across the past two campaigns for Barca and is an incredibly malleable asset, able to play off either wing or as a false nine. Add to that his advantage in experience having already played in the Premier League and his signature suddenly becomes that much more desirable.

‌



Alex Scott reunion pathway cleared

View 2 Images Alex Scott has turned down a Bournemouth contract extension for the second time so far this year (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

Alex Scott's chances of securing a move away from Bournemouth have increased after he turned down a new contract. It's reportedly the second time in 2026 the English playmaker has rejected fresh terms at the Vitality Stadium.

Scott, 22, formed a strong connection with Iraola during their time together on the south coast. The new Liverpool chief has spoken highly of Scott in the past and would possess a key advantage in any bidding war to snag his services.

Article continues below

Sky Sports News reported Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea are ahead of Liverpool in the hunt. And midfield doesn't appear to be a major priority for Liverpool right now, particularly given there's greater need for new faces down the right side.

However, with just two years remaining on his contract, this could be the big opportunity to get Scott on board if Iraola desires. The former Bristol City star is purportedly valued at north of £80m, with Bournemouth facing a dilemma over whether to capitalise now or risk losing their star for a heavily reduced fee in future.
