World.title: Gallery: Playful hats pop up on Tartu statues for British artist's new show
World.content:
Colorful hats and masks have appeared on prominent Tartu statues, heralding the opening of British artist Monster Chetwynd's first show at the Estonian National Museum (ERM).

After a successful run at Copenhagen Contemporary, Chetwynd's "A Feather in Your Hat!" is bringing a colorful world of costumes, creatures and imagination to Tartu as ERM hosts the artist's first exhibition in the entire Baltic region.

With a distinctive DIY aesthetic that transforms everyday materials into so much more, Monster Chetwynd presents a spectacular total installation that combines humor, fantasy and grotesque elements to form an immersive space inviting visitors to step inside, play and become part of the work.

At its center is the Red Hat Shop, a new work created specifically for Copenhagen where visitors can transform themselves with hats, masks and performative gestures.

Installation view of Monster Chetwynd's "A Feather in Your Hat!" at the Copenhagen Contemporary. March 2026. Source: Anders Sune Berg

Shelves filled with strange faces and creatures lead to a "green monster stage," where anyone can step into a new version of themselves.

Born in London and now based in Zurich, Monster Chetwynd draws on anything from pop culture and folklore to surrealistic cinema and puppet theater for inspiration.

Per installations often combine recycled materials, epic stage designs and costumes and live performance, creating works that are at once humorous, theatrical and engaging.

Installation view of Monster Chetwynd's "A Feather in Your Hat!" at the Copenhagen Contemporary. March 2026. Source: Anders Sune Berg

The artist adopted the name Monster Chetwynd in 2018, after previously working under the names Spartacus Chetwynd and Marvin Gaye Chetwynd.

Nominated for the Turner Prize in 2012, ze has exhibited at leading institutions across the world, including recent shows in China and Austria.

Part of ERM's 10th anniversary program marking a decade since the opening of its Raadi campus, Monster Chetwynd's "A Feather in Your Hat!" opens July 24 and will run through January 24, 2027.

World.title: OpenAI reports ‘unprecedented’ autonomous hack by AI agents
World.content:
San Francisco – ChatGPT maker OpenAI said Tuesday that its advanced artificial intelligence models had gone rogue during security testing, hacking into a popular platform for programmers on their own.

The San Francisco firm called it an “unprecedented cyber incident” and said it would conduct a joint investigation with the online code library Hugging Face.

AI models that underpin tools like chatbots and image generators are known as agents when they act autonomously to carry out tasks in the real world.

As the technology quickly becomes more sophisticated, cybersecurity is in the spotlight given the risk of advanced AI finding weak points in existing software before humans do.

OpenAI said the incident involved a combination of models, including its recently launched GPT-5.6 Sol “and an even more capable pre-release model”.

The company was trying to assess the models’ hacking capabilities by setting tasks in a tightly controlled digital testing ground, where internet access was limited for safety.

“While operating in our sandboxed testing environment, our models spent a substantial amount of (computing power) finding a way to obtain open Internet access, in pursuit of solving the evaluation problem,” an OpenAI blog about the incident said.

After connecting to the internet, the models decided to target the platform Hugging Face — a large repository of AI models, datasets and other information — to help in their quest.

Searching for “secret information” that could help it cheat the evaluation, the OpenAI system “chained together multiple attack vectors, including using stolen credentials”.

– ‘Catastrophic’ potential –

Hussein Abbass, a computing professor at UNSW Canberra, told AFP that the incident was “amazing on many fronts”.

“It did not just attack Hugging Face. It actually attacked its internal system to exploit its own vulnerabilities,” Abbass said.

“And that’s scary.”

GPT-5.6 and other cutting-edge models, including the Mythos series from OpenAI’s archrival Anthropic, have drawn concern over their potential to breach cybersecurity defences.

Both the US firms had to temporarily withhold the general release of these latest technologies because of fears in Washington that they could help break into crucial infrastructure.

Advanced AI is “normally in the hands of people who are ethical and responsible”, Abbass said.

But “it’s going to be catastrophic if it gets in someone’s hands with the intention to cause harm”.

How to govern the AI sector has become a key question, and “we need a community effort to manage this situation”, he added.

Hugging Face had reported the cyber “intrusion” last week, without mentioning OpenAI.

“This one was different from anything we had handled before in one important way: it was driven, end to end, by an autonomous AI agent system — and we detected and dissected it largely with AI of our own,” Hugging Face said.

Clement Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, said on X that the company had suspected the cyberattack had come from a world-leading AI lab, given the sophistication of the agent.

“We strongly believe there was no malicious intent on their part,” Delangue wrote, referring to OpenAI.

“It’s quite mind-blowing that all of this happened autonomously!”

World.title: Iraq to establish funding structure for Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed on Tuesday the establishment of a defined structure to finance and implement the strategic project of the Development Road, assuring the start of practical steps within a planned timeline.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in Baghdad with Turkish Minister of Transport and Infrastructure Abdulkadir Uraloglu, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The meeting addressed the project’s economic significance for Iraq, Turkey, and the region, as well as its role in improving economic integration and regional connectivity.

Uraloglu underscored Turkey’s strong interest in the project, highlighting that both parties recognize the necessity of developing its fundamental infrastructure.

In early June, Head of the state-owned General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Farhan al-Fartousi, said that the planning process for the project and the al-Faw Grand Port has made tremendous progress, with essential operating plans already submitted to the government.

The project will enter the implementation phase following government approval in the coming months, according to al-Fartousi.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

In 2024, Iraq, Turkey, the UAE, and Qatar signed a quadripartite agreement focused on Iraq’s Development Road project. This agreement aims to enhance cooperation on this strategic initiative, with the four countries collaborating to develop the necessary frameworks for its implementation.

Later in 2024, Turkey formed a council involving Bulgaria, Hungary, and Serbia to arrange the connection of Europe with Iraq’s Development Road.

As a global corridor for commodity and energy transportation, the project is projected to draw international trade while also providing significant job and investment opportunities for Iraq and countries in the region.

World.title: US-Iran strikes: latest developments
World.content:
Dubai – Iran and US forces traded new military attacks Tuesday, with Tehran warning of “more decisive and powerful” strikes ahead as the conflict threatened to widen with a blockade of Saudi ports by Houthi rebels in Yemen.

Here are the latest developments on Wednesday:

– Rubio warns ‘dangerous precedent’ over Hormuz –

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Southeast Asian foreign ministers on Wednesday that Iranian control of the Strait of Hormuz would set a dangerous precedent with repercussions beyond the Middle East.

“If we create a precedent in the Middle East where a nation-state can decide to control an international waterway, charge a toll and blow up your ships if you don’t pay, we have created a very dangerous precedent that will repeat itself in other parts of the world, including this region,” Rubio told envoys at a Manila gathering of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

He added that the United States remains “open” to diplomacy with Iran but that Tehran is not “serious”.

– New US attacks on Iran –

US Central Command said Tuesday it had completed an 11th consecutive night of strikes on military targets in Iran as the Middle East war intensified.

US forces targeted military infrastructure to “further degrade Iran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz,” CENTCOM posted on X.

– Trump vows to help Lebanon –

US President Donald Trump met his Lebanese counterpart Joseph Aoun at the White House, where he vowed to support the country with disarming Iran-backed Hezbollah and forging a lasting peace with Israel.

“President Aoun stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory,” according to a readout of the meeting from the Lebanese presidency.

After the talks, Trump said he would authorize the resumption of direct flights by US airlines to Lebanon, which have been suspended since the 1985 hijacking by Lebanese Islamist militants of a TWA flight with many Americans aboard.

– War cost US $37.5 billion –

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Iran war has cost the United States $37.5 billion so far, up from a previous estimate of nearly $29 billion in mid-May.

“The estimate we have as of today is $37.5 billion,” Hegseth told lawmakers during a congressional hearing Tuesday where he defended a request for $67 billion in supplemental funding for the Pentagon.

– Trump ‘not finished’ with Iran –

Trump said the United States will continue attacks on Iran, while forecasting it would take the Islamic republic two decades or more to rebuild from current damage.

“If we left right now, it would take Iran 20, 25 years to rebuild. Okay, and we’re not finished at all…we’re not leaving right now,” he told reporters during his meeting with Lebanon’s Aoun.

– Trump warns Houthis –

Trump said he would “take care of” the Houthi rebels if the Iran-backed militant group follows through on its threatened blockade of Saudi ports.

“If something like that happens, we take care of it,” Trump told reporters.

– Pakistan PM urges restraint –

Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called for restraint from all warring sides during a meeting with Iran’s interior minister.

Sharif “urged all sides to exercise restraint and refrain from actions that could further destabilize the region”, a statement from his office said, adding that he told Iran’s Eskandar Momeni that Pakistan would continue to act as a mediator.

– Kuwait slams Iranian attacks –

Kuwait said Iran hit several power and water desalination plants Monday, causing fires in the fourth such attacks in as many days.

– Bahrain says intercepts Iran strikes –

Bahrain sounded sirens as the country’s military had said it intercepted the latest of a spate of Iranian attacks on the Gulf kingdom.

“The siren has been sounded, Citizens and residents are urged to remain calm and head to the nearest safe place,” the interior ministry said in a statement on X.

– Iran stops tankers in Hormuz –

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they stopped two “non-compliant oil tankers” attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz, after “explosions caused extensive fires aboard them,” state news agency IRNA reported.

World.title: 3 drones intercepted near US consulate in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security sources said on Tuesday that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, according to Reuters.

A separate source told Al-Arabiya News that two drones targeted a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

No casualties or damage resulting from the drone attack in Erbil have been reported.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

During the Middle East war, Iran and its allied Iraqi militias have targeted Iraqi Kurdistan, which hosts US soldiers as part of the international coalition fighting ISIS, foreign oil firms, and Iranian Kurdish opposition parties.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: AI boom lifts Mexico tech exports, complicating Trump trade goals
World.content:
Mexico City – The United States’ frenzied rush to build out AI infrastructure has boosted exports of Mexican technology, complicating President Donald Trump’s hand heading into trade negotiations.

Trump, who campaigned on boosting US manufacturing, hopes to narrow the trade deficit with Mexico during talks to update the USMCA free trade agreement, which kick off Tuesday in Mexico City.

But the dizzying rise in computer equipment exports from Mexico — the largest US trading partner — is doing the opposite.

Between January and April, Mexico tripled its sales of computer equipment to the United States compared to the same period last year, with exports topping $50 billion versus just $2.2 billion in imports, according to AFP calculations.

The sector now makes up 30 percent of all Mexican products shipped to the United States, overtaking the automotive industry as the largest component of exports.

“It’s a milestone largely driven by demand for advanced AI electronics,” Diego Flores, head of electronic and digital industries at Mexico’s Economy Ministry, told AFP.

The sector, which includes processing units and data center hardware, is not officially on the agenda for this round of negotiations.

– Explosive demand –

The most in-demand products are server racks that house AI processing cards — a key component for the data centers multiplying across the United States.

The main export hub is the Pacific state of Jalisco, dubbed the “Mexican Silicon Valley,” where an ecosystem of global industry giants and tech startups have set up shop, Flores said.

Taiwanese giant Foxconn assembles server racks in Jalisco, and serves as a strategic partner to US chip designer Nvidia.

In March, Foxconn announced $137 million in investments across two Mexican subsidiaries after estimating its production could double this year.

“The United States and Mexico will remain our primary production hubs,” Chief Executive Michael Chiang said, announcing the company would invest 30 percent more than in 2025 to expand its AI-related capacity.

Faced with booming demand, Flextronics, another tech manufacturer in Jalisco, even had to repurpose its parking lots to expand manufacturing capacity, Flores said.

Yet the boom comes amid a volatile political climate.

The Trump administration rejected a 16-year extension of the USMCA, opting instead for annual reviews with Mexico and Canada.

Washington is also continuing to push for more goods to be manufactured domestically, even as US reliance on imports from Mexico, Taiwan, and China to fuel its AI boom grows.

– ‘In the line of fire’ –

Could the thriving sector become Trump’s next tariff target?

“Nobody can say for sure,” Flores admitted. However, he expressed confidence that the sector might escape protectionist policies due to its immense strategic value to the United States.

Washington is also seeking to limit the use of Asian technology within North America, according to William Jackson, a chief emerging markets economist at Capital Economics.

“The Trump administration has to weigh the demand for these technologies and the need to stay at the forefront of AI development,” he told AFP, noting that “tariffs could prove counterproductive to that goal.”

But balancing the preservation of a booming industry with protectionist rhetoric puts the sector “very easily in the line of fire,” he warned.

That risk is heightened by the fact that Mexican manufacturers use components sourced from China and Taiwan, which Trump could view as a “backdoor” or Trojan horse for Asian technology entering the United States.

World.title: At least 41 dead in Guyana capsized ferry disaster
World.content:
Georgetown – At least 41 people died after a ferry capsized off the coast of Guyana over the weekend, the government said Tuesday.

The MV Barima was traveling from the capital Georgetown to Port Kaituma in Guyana’s inland Essequibo region when it flipped over on Saturday night.

A desperate search for survivors has been underway since early Sunday, with 77 people rescued so far and dozens more missing, according to authorities.

A government report released Tuesday revised the death toll from 27 to 41.

“A total of 41 bodies have now been recovered,” it stated.

“The first recovery for the day was made at 10:15 am (1415GMT), and 14 bodies have been retrieved as of 1 pm” Tuesday, it added.

There had earlier been confusion over how many were involved in the tragedy due to an inaccurate passenger manifest which listed 133 people aboard, Public Works Minister Juan Edghill said.

But on Tuesday, Prime Minister Mark Phillips said he was confident that 179 people had been on board when the accident occurred.

Two crew members aboard the aging ferry tested positive for marijuana after the incident, he told reporters Sunday, adding that an investigation was underway.

The ship began its journey in mid-afternoon and a distress call was received about eight hours later.

The ferry was built in 1939, according to the shipping website VesselFinder.

Boats typically travel by sea before reaching a river to arrive at Port Kaituma, which is located in the depths of a dense rainforest.

Guyana, a small English-speaking country at the northeast corner of South America, is locked in a territorial dispute with neighboring Venezuela over the oil-rich Essequibo region.

World.title: Iraqi Airways launches new digital data center for automation push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The management of Iraqi Airways has officially opened a new digital Data Center, marking a major step forward in its comprehensive digital transformation and electronic automation project.

Ahmed Abbas, Director of the Data Center, emphasized that the project builds upon the airline’s broader automation strategy. This plan aims to implement electronic systems across all company divisions and establish an integrated digital ecosystem.

By connecting all departments, branches, and operational units under a single, unified data center, the initiative will enhance information security, unify data management, boost operational efficiency, and ensure the sustainability of digital services.

Key Strategic Objectives

Core Digital Infrastructure: Serves as one of the airline’s most critical infrastructure upgrades, modernizing IT operations to align with global standards.

Accelerated Operations: Streamlines procedures, supports integrated electronic systems, and speeds up daily operational workflows.

Enhanced Service Quality: Leverages modern technology to elevate overall service standards and customer experiences.

Government Alignment: Fulfills national e-governance mandates and Council of Ministers decisions regarding digital transformation and infrastructure development.

By launching this centralized Data Center, Iraqi Airways continues to modernize its civil aviation infrastructure, bringing faster processing, improved security, and higher-quality digital services to both internal operations and passengers.

World.title: Trump ‘not finished’ with Iran as Tehran steps up strikes
World.content:
Tehran – President Donald Trump said Tuesday that the United States was not finished attacking Iran, as Tehran stepped up its strikes across the Middle East.

The US leader projected that it would take the Islamic republic more than 20 years to rebuild from damage sustained in the Middle East war, two weeks after fighting between the decades-old foes resumed.

“If we left right now, it would take Iran 20, 25 years to rebuild,” he said. “We’re not finished at all… we’re not leaving right now.”

His comments came after Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain came under attack Tuesday.

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels meanwhile said they would blockade Saudi Arabia’s ports, threatening to throw energy markets into chaos after Iran’s Strait of Hormuz blockade.

Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian attacks as sirens sounded multiple times in the kingdom, with Kuwait and Jordan also announcing they had intercepted drone and missile strikes.

Kuwait has said that Tehran hit multiple power and water desalination plants across the country over the past days, including on Monday, forcing residents to ration energy consumption.

Iran’s Guards confirmed a strike on Jordan, claiming they had targeted a “complex housing US terrorist forces in the region of Rukban”.

The Iranian army had earlier said it targeted US assets in Kuwait and Bahrain, including air defence systems, radar installations and administrative buildings.

“With this radar sweep, the enemy should prepare for even more decisive and powerful waves of drone and missile attacks,” the Guards said in a statement carried by state news agency IRNA.

– Houthi threat –

US President Donald Trump said he would “take care of” the Houthi rebels if the Iran-backed militant group followed through on its threatened blockade of Saudi ports.

“If something like that happens, we take care of it,” Trump said. “You know, we’ve done that with the Houthis before, and we haven’t heard from them in a while since we did what we did originally.”

Saudi Arabia strongly condemned the threat from what it called the “terrorist Houthi militia” and said it “continues to support the brotherly Yemeni people and their legitimate government”.

It remains unclear how the Houthis would implement their blockade of Saudi ports, and oil markets eased slightly despite the threat from Iran’s ally against the world’s biggest crude exporter.

But maritime intelligence provider Vanguard Tech said a Singapore-flagged tanker and a Liberia-flagged tanker both “reversed course” in the Red Sea after loading crude at the Saudi port of Yanbu following the Houthi warning.

Should the Houthis make good on their threat to blockade Saudi ports, that would put at risk Riyadh’s ability to bypass Hormuz for some of its oil exports and have major repercussions for the global economy.

Saudi Arabia and the Houthis traded fire last week for the first time in years, threatening a 2022 truce in their years-long conflict, but the rebels have largely remained on the sidelines since Israel and the US attacked Iran in late February.

The Revolutionary Guards said on Tuesday that two tankers attempting to transit Hormuz “were hit by explosions, resulting in massive fires that brought them to a standstill”.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) earlier reported that an “unknown projectile” struck a tanker off the coast of Oman.

– ‘Still struggling’ –

Following the deaths of at least three US soldiers in recent days, the US launched a new round of attacks against Iran on Monday it said was “designed to further degrade Iranian military capabilities used to attack commercial shipping” in the Strait of Hormuz.

The deaths bring to 17 the number of fatalities among US service members. Nearly 100 US service members have been wounded since war resumed on July 7, the Pentagon said Monday.

Shahin, a 34-year-old embroiderer from Iranshahr in southeast Iran, said: “We’re still struggling to secure our most basic life necessities, and now we’re dealing with destruction from the war on top of it.”

As Iran stepped up its attacks in the Gulf, Kuwait’s foreign ministry on Tuesday said it had summoned Iran’s ambassador over a strike against a ship passing through the Hormuz strait the day before.

Despite the latest fighting, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said diplomatic exchanges with Washington via mediators were ongoing.

Mediator Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called for restraint from all warring sides during a meeting with Iran’s Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni on Tuesday.

Sharif urged the sides to “refrain from actions that could further destabilise the region”, his office said.

World.title: J&K: Terrorists kill Amarnath Yatra security personnel in Anantnag attack
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A police personnel was killed after terrorists attacked a police party in

's Anantnag town on Wednesday, officials told news agency PTI.

The attack took place around 12.30 pm near Lal Chowk in Anantnag town, when the assailants fired at the police team, officials said.

Head Constable Ashiq Hussain, who was deployed on Amarnath Yatra security duty, sustained critical injuries in the attack and was rushed to the Government Medical College (GMC) Hospital in Anantnag, officials said.

Doctors declared him dead on arrival, they added.

Following the attack, security forces cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to trace the assailants.

Meanwhile, The Resistance Front (TRF), a proxy outfit of the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), claimed responsibility for the attack through a post on social media, according to officials.

Further details are awaited.

In a separate incident, an Army personnel died after accidentally falling from a height near the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir's Rajouri district on Wednesday, officials said.

The deceased, identified as Rifleman Sukhpreet Singh (27), was on operational duty at the forward Mahadev post in the Sunderbani sector when he reportedly lost his balance and fell from a height, resulting in fatal injuries, officials said.





His body was shifted to a hospital for post-mortem examination. Police have initiated inquest proceedings, officials added.

Following the completion of legal formalities, the soldier's mortal remains will be taken to his native place in Punjab, where he will be accorded the last rites.

World.title: SC issues notice to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla against approval of Sena (UBT) MPs' merger with Shinde faction
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notices to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the Lok Sabha Secretary and six rebel Shiv Sena MPs on a plea filed by the Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray (UBT) faction challenging the Speaker's decision to recognise the merger of the six MPs with the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.

The top court has further posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.

The plea was filed by UBT MP Arvind Ganpat Sawant against the Speaker's decision, which was approved ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament. A bench comprising Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe issued notice to the respondents while refusing to stay the Speaker's order at this stage.

Moved to SC earlier

The Shiv Sena (UBT) on Tuesday approached the Supreme Court challenging Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's decision to approve the merger of its six MPs with the Shiv Sena led by Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde.

Senior advocate Devadatt Kamat, appearing for the Uddhav Thackeray-led party, mentioned the matter before a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M. Pancholi, seeking an urgent hearing on Wednesday.

Merger alters Lok Sabha numbers

Ahead of the Monsoon Session, Speaker Om Birla approved the merger of six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs with the Shinde-led Shiv Sena.

The MPs are Sanjay Deshmukh (Yavatmal), Sanjay Jadhav (Parbhani), Sanjay Dina Patil (Mumbai North East), Nagesh Patil-Ashtikar (Hingoli), Omprakash Rajenimbalkar (Dharashiv) and Bhausaheb Wakchaure (Shirdi).





With the merger, the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena's strength in the Lok Sabha has come down to three MPs, while the Shinde-led Shiv Sena's tally has increased to 13 MPs, making it the third-largest constituent of the NDA after the BJP and the Telugu Desam Party (TDP).

Reacting to the development, Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde said the six MPs joined his party to secure development for their constituencies and not for "personal gains".

World.title: Bhojshala row: SC to hear Muslim side's plea on alternate namaz site on Friday
World.content:
Poll Vote & Share your view How far should alternate prayer sites be from the disputed complex? Within 500 meters No limit, as long as there's a site 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The Supreme Court agreed to hear the Muslim side's plea in the dispute involving the Bhojshala complex in Dhar on Friday after the petitioners alleged that the alternate site identified by the Madhya Pradesh government for offering Friday namaz is too far from the disputed complex.On Tuesday, a Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked solicitor general Tushar Mehta to obtain instructions from the Madhya Pradesh government on the possibility of providing an alternate prayer site adjacent to the disputed complex.Appearing for the Muslim side, senior advocate Huzefa Ahmadi submitted that the court's earlier order had directed the state to provide an open space near the Bhojshala site for offering prayers. However, he alleged that the land identified by the authorities was around 2 km away."The order was that land should be near the Bhojshala site. The land given for Friday prayer is 2 km away. We have already missed Friday prayers," Ahmadi told the Bench, news agency PTI reported.Responding on behalf of the Madhya Pradesh government, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said the alternate site was approximately 900 metres from the disputed complex.He assured the court that he would personally verify the issue. "I will personally look into this and rectify it," Mehta said, acccording to PTI.Justice Bagchi underlined that the court's previous directions must be implemented as intended. "The court's earlier order has to be followed in letter and spirit," Justice Bagchi observed.The Bench thereafter agreed to list the matter for hearing on Friday and directed the solicitor general to seek instructions from the state government regarding the provision of an "adjacent site" for offering namaz.The issue arises from the Supreme Court's interim order of July 14, when it heard appeals filed by the Muslim side against the Madhya Pradesh high court's judgment declaring the disputed Bhojshala complex a temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati.In that order, the apex court directed the state government to provide Muslims with a separate open space adjacent to the disputed site for offering Friday namaz between 1 pm and 3 pm until the matter is finally decided.The Bench had clarified that the arrangement would remain ad hoc and subject to the final outcome of the petitions. It also directed the Archaeological Survey of India not to carry out any structural changes at the disputed site without prior permission from the court.While passing the interim directions, the Supreme Court urged restraint from both communities, observing that Bhojshala was a sensitive dispute. The court also indicated its readiness to hear the matter on a day-to-day basis if necessary.

World.title: 'Don't have time to watch videos': CJI Surya Kant declines intervention in Jantar Mantar protest crackdown
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Wednesday declined a request for an urgent hearing of a petition challenging the alleged "police brutality" against students at Jantar Mantar saying, "we do not have time to watch videos.

"

The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant-led bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.

Seeking an urgent listing, the petitioner's counsel told the court that students had allegedly been subjected to police brutality during Monday's protest and said the plea contained three prayers.

"I have the videos as well regarding police brutality... If it can be listed tomorrow (Thursday)...

students are there," the lawyer submitted.

The CJI, however, declined the request saying, "We are not interested in videos, we don't have time to watch... We don't want to watch videos."

When the counsel again referred to the video evidence and alleged that students had been beaten up, the CJI responded, "Don't waste our time. We don't want to watch any videos," according to news agency PTI.

The petition relates to the police action during theCockroach Janta Party's (CJP) 'Sansad Chalo' march on Monday, the opening day of Parliament's Monsoon Session.





Thousands of students and young protesters had marched towards Parliament demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations.

The protest turned violent after demonstrators attempted to breach police barricades. Security personnel used lathis and tear gas to disperse the crowd, with both protesters and police reporting injuries.

Meanwhile, the CJP's sit-in at Jantar Mantar entered its second month on Wednesday, with the organisation claiming that more supporters joined the protest overnight.

Volunteers at the protest site continued receiving food and other supplies sent by supporters, even as heavy security remained deployed in the area following Monday's clashes.

The agitation began on June 20, with protesters seeking accountability over alleged examination irregularities, reforms in the education system and the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Activist Sonam Wangchuk, who joined the protest on June 28, continues his indefinite hunger strike from Medanta Hospital after being shifted there from Safdarjung Hospital following a Delhi high court order.

Wangchuk has said he will continue his fast until accountability is fixed in the education system or political leaders assure him that the issue will be taken up in Parliament.

These development come months after CJI Surya Kant while hearing a separate case likened some unemployed youngsters to "cockroaches", saying they end up becoming media persons, social media users and RTI activists.

"There are youngsters like cockroaches, who don't get any employment and don't have any place in the profession. Some of them become media, some of them become social media, some of them become RTI activists, some of them become other activists, and they start attacking everyone," he had said.

The remarks were made in an unrelated case in which a lawyer had challenged the Delhi high court's process for designating senior advocates. The CJI later clarified that his remarks aimed at people allegedly entering the legal profession with "fake and bogus degrees."

World.title: NEET protest: Rahul Gandhi, opposition wear black in Parliament day after PM residence protest- watch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

, along with MPs from the INDIA bloc, arrived in Parliament on Wednesday dressed in black to mark a "Black Day" over the alleged NEET irregularities and the police action against protesting students.

Congress MP

, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra, JMM MP Mahua Maji and several other opposition leaders also wore black as they gathered at Makar Dwar to stage a protest on the third day of Monsoon session of Parliament. The MPs raised slogans demanding justice for students and the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the controversy surrounding the examination.

Opposition reacts

Akhilesh Yadav questioned why the government was unwilling to remove the Union education minister, asking,"What pressure is the government under that it cannot remove the minister?" Explaining the Opposition's decision to wear black in Parliament, he said,"We have come wearing black clothes. Black is the colour of protest; it is also the colour of grief."

JMM MP Mahua Maji, while talking to reporters, said that the goal was to protect students, not score political points.





"Opposition stands unitedâ, she said.

Congress leaders Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Mallikarjun Kharge also launched a sharp attack on the Centre during the Opposition's "Black Day" protest in Parliament.

Speaking to reporters, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said the focus should remain on the students' demands rather than the treatment meted out to Opposition leaders. "What happened with us is irrelevant. Students have genuine demands and are asking for their rights," she said.

She alleged that despite an education budget of Rs 1.4 lakh crore, the government had "waived off Rs 16 lakh crore loans for Adani and Ambani," while students continued to face repeated paper leaks. "Students have a genuine struggle and are asking for change. Paper leaks are happening repeatedly. There is nothing undemocratic about peaceful protest, but what is happening with students and in Parliament is undemocratic," she added.

Congress president and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge also accused the Centre of undermining democratic institutions. "They are functioning like a dictatorship. They do not respect MPs. They harass even those who protest as per rules," he said.

Kharge further alleged that BJP-RSS workers were operating alongside the police and warned the government against attempting to intimidate the opposition.

World.title: 'Does India run on your arrogance?' BJP tears into Rahul Gandhi over PM residence march
World.content:
BJP calls Rahul's march to PM residence 'irresponsible conduct'

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority to prevent paper leaks in competitive exams? Enhanced security measures Strict action against offenders Better transparency in exam processes 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: A day after Rahul Gandhi's march to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence ended in a confrontation with police, the BJP mounted a sharp political counteroffensive on Wednesday, accusing Lok Sabha leader of opposition of disregarding the dignity of the Prime Minister's residence and announcing nationwide protests against Congress party.The saffron party also called out Rahul Gandhi's "Chalo PM Residence" as "irresponsible" and "highly condemnable." Leading the attack, senior party leader Ravi Shankar Prasad asked Lok Sabha LoP: "'Does this country run on your arrogance?"Addressing a presser in New Delhi, senior BJP leader and former Union minister Ravi Shankar Prasad took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi's political legacy, saying that someone from a family that produced three Prime Ministers should have understood the dignity attached to the Prime Minister's residence."He is sitting on a dharna at the gate of the Prime Minister's residence. His father Rajiv Gandhi was the Prime Minister, his grandmother Indira Gandhi was the Prime Minister, and his great-grandfather Jawaharlal Nehru was also the Prime Minister of India. He, of all people, should know the dignity and sanctity of the Prime Minister's residence. Despite this, the kind of irresponsible behaviour he has displayed is highly condemnable," Prasad said.Announcing the BJP's response, Prasad said the saffron party would stage protests across the country outside Congress offices."The BJP will hold protests today across the country against Congress outside Congress offices for the unruly protest outside the PM's house yesterday," he said.Questioning Rahul Gandhi's approach, Prasad accused the Congress leader of abandoning dialogue and trying to dictate terms to the government."How do you intend to function? Will you just sit there forcibly? You were engaged in a dialogue. They were ready for a debate on the NEET issue, but then you backed out. Does this country run on your stick? Will it run on your arrogance? Rahul Gandhi, you have been irresponsible. I condemn your entire conduct," he said.Defending the police action during the protest, the BJP leader said security personnel had no option but to intervene to maintain law and order in the high-security zone."Later, the police were forced to take action, which was necessary for security and for maintaining peace. The Prime Minister has always been clear on these issues," Prasad said.Shifting focus to the controversy surrounding competitive examinations, Prasad asserted that the government had acted swiftly to protect the integrity of recruitment and entrance tests."In the past, irregularities were reported in several states during various examinations. Consequently, foolproof exams were conducted immediately after cancellations. The results have been declared with a 56-57% success rate, and students are satisfied. These exams were held without charging any additional fees," he told reporters.Emphasising the Centre's commitment to students, Prasad said those responsible for exam irregularities had been arrested and were facing trial."All the candidates appearing for NEET and other exams are our children. It is our duty to be concerned about their future, and we will fulfill that responsibility. Those involved in irregularities have been arrested and are facing trial. The government is ensuring that their trial leads to certain punishment," he said.The senior BJP leader concluded by reiterating Prime Minister Narendra Modi's assurance that the sanctity of NEET and other examinations would be protected through systemic reforms and stricter scrutiny.Meanwhile, another voice from the ruling BJP joined the attack on Rahul Gandhi. Senior BJP leader and MP Giriraj Singh told reporters, "Rahul Gandhi has tarnished the dignity of the Constitution while holding a constitutional position. His conduct is extremely dangerous. A case of sedition should be filed against Rahul Gandhi."The BJP's attack came a day after Rahul led the Opposition's march towards Lok Kalyan Marg, the official residence of the Prime Minister, where protesters came face-to-face with security personnel in the high-security Lutyens' Delhi zone.Videos from the scene showed police moving in to disperse the protesters gathered outside the Prime Minister's residence. In one video shared by the Congress on its official X handle, Rahul Gandhi was seen lying on the road as police personnel attempted to lift and remove him from the protest site. The former Congress president appeared to resist being taken away as security officials surrounded him.The Congress also released a photograph showing Rahul nosebleed following the police action, alleging excessive use of force during the protest.Rahul Gandhi's protest came amid Jantar Mantar protest demanding Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over accountability in the NEET paper-leak.

World.title: 'Main bhi cockroach': Student protests against NEET reach New York, London - watch
World.content:
Protests spread to London

Protest continues at Jantar Mantar

Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)

NEW DELHI: New York witnessed demonstrations in support of 'cockroaches', on Tuesday, as students and members of Indian diaspora rallied over alleged irregularities in the NEET examinations.The protesters gathered at the Mahatma Gandhi statue in New York City's Union Square carrying placards in support of students.Similar solidarity demonstrations were held in London, where protesters gathered outside the Indian High Commission in support of the nationwide movement demanding accountability over the alleged NEET irregularities and reforms in India's education system.Holding placards and raising slogans, the demonstrators expressed support and called for greater transparency, accountability and reforms in the country's examination and education system.Manchester, Berlin and Netherlands also witnessed protest demading Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.Jantar Mantar continues to witness thousands of protesters on Wesneday days after the 'Sansad Chalo' march on July 20, as the agitation over alleged irregularities in the NEET examinations showed no signs of slowing down.On Tuesday, thecalled off its proposed sit-in outside the Delhi Police headquarters after claiming that all protesters detained following the march had been released. The outfit had earlier alleged that hundreds of its supporters were being held in custody and denied access to legal counsel, a charge that was rejected by the Delhi Police.Meanwhile, opposition parties have extended support to Wangchuk's agitation and staged protests in the national capital, demanding accountability over the alleged irregularities in the conduct of the NEET examination.

World.title: Daughter in SC, seeks return of Netaji's ashes from Japan
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Three months after a failed attempt by his grandnephew, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's octogenarian Germany-based daughter, Anita Pfaff, moved Supreme Court Tuesday seeking a direction to govt to bring his ashes back from the Renko-Ji temple in Japan.

Pfaff's petition, settled by senior advocate A M Singhvi, complained of "India's prolonged failure to take a final, reasoned and time-bound decision" to repatriate to India the "mortal remains/ashes attributed to Netaji, preserved at Renko-Ji temple" to allow the sole living direct lineal descendant to perform his last rites with dignity and finality.

"There is gross delay," said a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi.

However, it adjourned the hearing on Pfaff's petition on finding the arguing counsel absent.

Ahead of the West Bengal assembly elections, a petition was filed in SC by Netaji's gr-andnephew, Ashis Ray, seeking the same direction to the Centre. Appearing for Ray, Singhvi had argued before the bench of the same three judges on March 12 that the petition had the support of Pfaff, who joined the proceedings virtually.

Singhvi had said the fact that every head of state from India, over decades, had paid obeisance at Renko-Ji temple was proof that the freedom fighter's ashes were there.





The CJI-led bench had said there was no doubt that he was one of the country's greatest freedom fighters, but refused to entertain Ray's plea.

Justice Bagchi had said, "We respect her (Pfaff's) sentiments and we will ensure that her sentiments are translated into legal action. But she must step forward."

Singhvi had withdrawn the petition. Heeding SC's suggestion, Pfaff filed the petition seeking repatriation of Netaji's ashes by India or, as an alternative, "facilitate her to repatriate the ashes".

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: No moral right to offer advice on peaceful protests, CJP's Dipke tells Delhi Police
World.content:
People, including supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), continue to join the sit-in at Jantar Mantar on Wednesday (July 22, 2026), with the CJP saying “millions more will come” to Delhi if the government doesn’t agree to its demands, primarily the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET ‘paper’ leak issue. The CJP leadership, led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, have highlighted a demand following the July 20 ‘Chalo Sansad’ march that no FIR or future FIR should be lodged against any protester.

Also read: Police file four FIRs amid flak over crackdown on protesters

Meanwhile, the Supreme Court on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) declined a request for urgent listing of a plea challenging the police action against students during the CJP protest march in Delhi on July 20. “We are not interested in videos, we don’t have time to watch... We don’t want to watch videos,” the CJI said, declining the request.

A total of 20 CRPF companies are being airlifted from Kolkata to be deployed in Delhi to strengthen the law and order in view of the CJP protests, demonstrations by various political parties and the ongoing Parliament session, officials said.

Also read: Hundreds of people order food online for protestors at Jantar Mantar

Union Ministers J.P. Nadda and Dr. Jitendra Singh visited activist Sonam Wangchuk - who is on day 25 of his indefinite fast - at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram after he was moved there in compliance with the Delhi High Court order. Urging him to appeal to students to keep faith and avoid further escalation, the Ministers also conveyed the government’s decision to initiate a debate in Parliament, sources said. On Wednesday (July 22, 2026), Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju informed the Lok Sabha of the government’s willingness to take up a discussion on the NEET paper ‘leak’ issue.

World.title: SC directs Centre, MP to comply with order on namaz site near Bhojshala complex ‘in letter and spirit’
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) directed the Union and Madhya Pradesh governments to comply “in letter and spirit” with its July 14 order requiring the authorities to identify a separate open space near the disputed Bhojshala-Kamal Maula Mosque complex where members of the Muslim community could offer Friday namaz between 1 p.m. and 3 p.m. as an interim arrangement. The direction came after the court was informed that the site identified by the administration was nearly two kilometres away.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the authorities were under an obligation to carry out its earlier directions in their entirety. The matter has been listed again on Friday for the court to review compliance.

The matter was mentioned before the Bench by senior advocate Huzefa Ahmadi, appearing for the Muslim petitioners, who submitted that the location identified by the authorities for offering Friday namaz was nearly 2 km from the disputed complex. “They have earmarked a place two kilometres away from the site,” Mr. Ahmadi told the court.

Also Read | Bhojshala case: Madhya Pradesh High Court refers to 10 principles laid down by Supreme Court in Ayodhya verdict

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and the Madhya Pradesh government, however, pointed out that the earmarked space for offering namaz was about 900 m away from the disputed site. He also apprised the Bench that he had already conveyed to the authorities to identify an alternative site.

“I had a word with the authorities and it is 900 m away. But I am in talks with them and have asked them to identify an alternative site,” Mr. Mehta said.

Justice Bhagchi, however, reminded the law officer that the expression used in the interim order was “adjacent site”. “Last time when we used the expression ‘adjacent site’...”, the judge said.

The law officer assured the court that he had already spoken to the authorities and that the issue would be resolved soon. “That order will be taken care of. I have already spoken to the authorities there,” he submitted.

The Bench, however, made it clear that there could be no deviation from its earlier directions. “The order has to be complied with in letter and spirit”, it said while agreeing to list the matter on Friday.

The dispute concerns the Bhojshala Temple-Kamal Maula Mosque complex in Madhya Pradesh’s Dhar district, where both Hindu and Muslim communities have long asserted competing religious claims.

On July 14, the apex court had refrained from restoring status quo ante after the Madhya Pradesh High Court declared that the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula Mosque complex was a temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati and barred Friday namaz at the site. The court had reasoned that it did not want to “create tension” in a “very sensitive” issue.

The Bench further prohibited the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) from allowing any structural alterations to be made to the disputed structure without the prior permission of the apex court. The court issued formal notice to the State of Madhya Pradesh and the Union government.

“Let us not pass any order which creates tension. We are ready to hear the case on a day-to-day basis and resolve the issue. We request both sides to have patience. It is only a matter of a few days,” Chief Justice Kant had assured the Muslim appellants.

On May 15, the Madhya Pradesh High Court ruled that the disputed Bhojshala-Kamal Maula Mosque complex in Dhar district was a temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati. It had simultaneously quashed a decades-old ASI order that had allowed the Muslim community to offer Friday prayers at the site. The High Court had also said that the Centre and the ASI could decide on the Bhojshala complex’s administration and management.

The Hindu community considers Bhojshala a temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati, while the Muslim side calls the 11th-century monument the Kamal Maula Mosque. The disputed complex is protected by the ASI.

World.title: Chittoor police arrest 42-year-old in POCSO case within a day
World.content:
Chittoor district police on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) night arrested a 42-year-old man within 24 hours of registering a case for alleged sexual assault on a minor girl in Bangarupalyam mandal, Superintendent of Police Tushar Dudi said.

According to the police, the incident took place on July 17. The minor disclosed the alleged assault to her parents, following which her mother lodged a complaint at the Bangarupalyam police station on the night of July 20.

Based on the complaint, the police registered a case under Sections 65(1), 75(2), 78(2) and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 4 read with Section 3(a) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.

Special police teams working under the supervision of Deputy SP (Palamaner) Degala Prabhakar arrested the accused near the Paleru flyover on the night of July 21. He was later remanded in judicial custody. The SP commended the Bangarupalyam police team for its swift action.

World.title: World is ‘extremely turbulent’, Jaishankar calls for deeper India-ASEAN cooperation
World.content:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) said that the world is "extremely turbulent", and it is evident that "no single nation" or "even grouping" can deal with it on its own, underlining the need for deeper cooperation between India and ASEAN.

India-ASEAN ties making steady progress: Modi

Mr. Jaishankar, who is on a two-day visit to Manila to attend a meeting of the Quad grouping as well as to participate in deliberations under the framework of the ASEAN bloc, also acknowledged the role of the Philippines as the country coordinator in further strengthening the India-ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

The theme, ‘Navigating Our Future Together’, “captures the sentiment which many of us feel today. The world is extremely turbulent, and it is increasingly evident that no single nation or even grouping can deal with it on its own,” the External Affairs Minister said during his opening remarks at the ASEAN Post-Ministerial Conference with India 2026 on Wednesday (July 22, 2026).

"Let us contemplate the near future and consider how best our cooperation can serve our respective interests. In this era of volatility and disruption, the most visible stress is on supply chains," he added.

ASEAN’s top diplomats meet in shadow of U.S.-Iran conflict

"Energy, food and health security can no longer be taken for granted. Because we are all so dependent on maritime trade, that too could become a source of anxiety. Observing international law in that regard is therefore vital. Coincidentally, 2026 is the ASEAN-India year of maritime cooperation," he said.

The ASEAN, or the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, is considered one of the most influential groupings in the region, and India and several other countries, including the U.S., China, Japan and Australia, are its dialogue partners.

Myanmar tells ASEAN Aung San Suu Kyi will be looked after: envoy

"It is a timely reminder of what we can do for a more stable and secure future. At the same time, both India and ASEAN are optimistic about their prospects. Our eyes must therefore be firmly fixed on opportunities, even while addressing challenges."

He further said that the India-ASEAN agenda covers trade and investment, mobility and talent, tech, digital and AI, green and sustainability, as well as connectivity.

"It is only through deeper cooperation that we can de-risk and diversify." "India and ASEAN have traditionally worked for the welfare of the larger region... This is a world in transition, and India and ASEAN, who account for 2 billion, must navigate it together if it is to remain safe and steady," Mr. Jaishankar said.

World.title: ‘Don’t waste our time’: CJI Kant declines to take cognisance of police violence during CJP’s Parliament march
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) declined to initiate suo motu proceedings to take cognisance of alleged police excesses during the July 20 crackdown on student protesters in the national capital. When a lawyer submitted that there was videographic evidence of police brutality against the protesters, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant orally declined to examine the videos, saying that the court’s time should not be “wasted”.

Jantar Mantar protest LIVE updates - July 22, 2026

Mentioning the matter before a Bench headed by the Chief Justice, the lawyer urged the court to take cognisance of the alleged police violence against the student protesters.

He pointed out that thousands of students had gathered for the “Chalo Sansad” protest organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), demanding fair entrance examinations, reforms in the National Testing Agency (NTA), and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination paper leaks.

“The protest is already going on in Jantar Mantar. The police are already taking brutal actions,” the lawyer submitted.

The Chief Justice, however, cut him short. “Don’t waste our time, and don’t waste your time,” he told the lawyer.

The lawyer nevertheless attempted to persuade the Bench, submitting that the protest centred on issues affecting lakhs of students, including the conduct of the NEET examination and reforms in the NTA. “Students are seeking three very important prayers — that NEET examinations should be conducted in a free and fair manner by the government... Certainly, the NTA should be dissolved,” he added.

As the Bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohan, indicated that it was not inclined to hear him further, the lawyer said he had a collection of videos purportedly showing police personnel assaulting unarmed protesters and offered to place them before the court.

“We are not interested in videos. We don’t have time to watch them,” the Chief Justice observed, declining the request for an urgent hearing.

The apex court’s observations came a day after Delhi High Court Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya also refused to grant an urgent hearing on a plea alleging excessive use of force by the Delhi Police during the Monday protests. Declining the request for immediate listing, the Chief Justice remarked, “Don’t drag the Court into this. It will come up tomorrow.”

The Chief Justice’s reported remark on “cockroach” in reference to fake law degree holders during the hearing of a writ petition on May 15 spawned public furore and a viral online platform, the Cockroach Janta Party, which is spearheading the protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. The Chief Justice had offered a “clarification” the following day in a statement that he was misquoted by sections of the media and had the greatest concern and respect for the youths of the country.

On Monday (July 20, 2026), the Delhi Police cracked down on the “Chalo Sansad” protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), leaving several protesters injured. The Hindu has reported that at least one of the nearly 80 protesters injured during the march to Parliament sustained pellet gun injuries and is undergoing treatment at Lady Hardinge Medical College.

The police action came amid an internet shutdown in the New Delhi district, even as CJP representatives Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka met Union Minister J.P. Nadda to formally seek the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

The police action has since sparked a political storm, with Opposition MPs protesting inside and outside Parliament before marching to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence on Tuesday (July 21, 2026). Alleging that the government had refused to allow a discussion on the issue in Parliament, they staged a sit-in outside the Prime Minister’s residence, following which the Delhi Police detained them.

Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi subsequently called on Prime Minister Modi to apologise to the students affected by the police crackdown. He also reiterated the Opposition’s demand for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 3 LIVE: Kiren Rijiju says government ready for discussion on NEET-UG paper leak issue
